parts.problemMd:
The diagram shows a prism of length $16\mathrm{cm}$.

![Diagram of a triangular prism. The cross-section of the prism is a right-angled triangle labelled ABC. AB is the base of 7 cm, BC is the perpendicular height of 6 cm and the length of the prism is 16 cm. 
There is one vertex labelled P in the bottom left corner](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/SyllabAI/syllabai-resources/3b2ce8da700b80f51700fb34fc721c90d6654d6b/SME-ExamQuestion/cie-igcse-maths-international-maths-23-extended/pythagoras-and-trigonometry/3d-pythagoras-and-trigonometry/assets/005-diagram-of-a-triangular-prism-the-cross-section-.png)

Triangle $ABC$ is a cross-section of the prism with $AB=7\mathrm{cm}$, $BC=6\mathrm{cm}$ and angle $ABC=90^{\circ}$.

Calculate the length of $PC$

............................ $\mathrm{cm}$
parts.solutionMd:
> *Start by identifying the length that you are being asked to find on the diagram*
*Highlight a right-angled triangle that includes this length*
*This will help you to identify which lengths you need to calculate*

![The original diagram from the question but with a right-angled triangle ACP highlighted. Angle PAC is a right angle.](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/SyllabAI/syllabai-resources/3b2ce8da700b80f51700fb34fc721c90d6654d6b/SME-ExamQuestion/cie-igcse-maths-international-maths-23-extended/pythagoras-and-trigonometry/3d-pythagoras-and-trigonometry/assets/006-the-original-diagram-from-the-question-but-with-.png)

> *Use Pythagoras' theorem, *$a^{2}+b^{2}=c^{2}$*, on the right-angled triangle *$ABC$*, to find the length *$AC$

$AC^{2}=AB^{2}+BC^{2}\,AC^{2}=7^{2}+6^{2}$

**[1]**

$AC=\sqrt{7^{2}+6^{2}}=\sqrt{85}$

> *Use Pythagoras' theorem, *$a^{2}+b^{2}=c^{2}$*, on the right-angled triangle *$ACP$*, to find the length *$PC$

$\begin{gathered} P C^{2} & = A C^{2} + A P^{2} \\ P C^{2} & = ( \sqrt{85} )^{2} + 16^{2} \end{gathered}$

**[1]**

$\begin{gathered} P C & = \sqrt{( \sqrt{85} )^{2} + 16^{2}} \end{gathered}$

**Final answer:** $18.5$** cm**

**Answers of **$18.46$** to **$18.47$** will also be accepted [1]**

The diagram shows a cuboid $PQRSTUVW$.

$PV=17.2\mathrm{cm}$

The angle between the line $PV$ and the base $TUVW$ of the cuboid is $43^{\circ}$. Calculate $PT$.

$PT=$ ........................................... cm
parts.solutionMd:
> *The line **PV, **the line **PT **and the angle **PVT  **form a right-angled triangle so SOHCAHTOA can be used to find the missing side **PT.*

> *Draw the sides of the triangle onto the diagram to make the right-angled triangle clearer.*

![cie-igcse-20120-oct-nov-p2-tz1-q21-working](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/SyllabAI/syllabai-resources/3b2ce8da700b80f51700fb34fc721c90d6654d6b/SME-ExamQuestion/cie-igcse-maths-international-maths-23-extended/pythagoras-and-trigonometry/3d-pythagoras-and-trigonometry/assets/052-cie-igcse-20120-oct-nov-p2-tz1-q21-working.png)

** Identifying the angle on the diagram correctly**** [1]**

> *The side opposite the angle is needed and the hypotenuse is known so use  *$\mathrm{sin}x^{\circ}=\frac{\mathrm{Opp}}{\mathrm{Hyp}}$*.*

$\mathrm{sin}43^{\circ}=\frac{PT}{17.2}$

**[1]**

> * Solve the trigonometric equation to find the side **PT.** *

$\begin{gathered} P T & = 17.2 \sin 43^{\circ} \\ = 11.7303... \end{gathered}$

**PT**** = 11.7 cm (3 s.f.)**** [1]**

parts.problemMd:
The diagram shows a cuboid $ABCDEFGH$.

![q19-4ma1-1h-qp-jan20-paper1-igcse-maths](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/SyllabAI/syllabai-resources/3b2ce8da700b80f51700fb34fc721c90d6654d6b/SME-ExamQuestion/cie-igcse-maths-international-maths-23-extended/pythagoras-and-trigonometry/3d-pythagoras-and-trigonometry/assets/014-q19-4ma1-1h-qp-jan20-paper1-igcse-maths.png)

$EH=9\mathrm{cm},HG=5\mathrm{cm}$  and     $GB=6\mathrm{cm}.$

Work out the size of the angle between $AH$ and the plane $EFGH$. 
Give your answer correct to 3 significant figures.
parts.solutionMd:
> *To identify the angle between a line and a plane it is helpful to draw a right angled triangle using the line that is perpendicular to the plane.*

![oJu1V9fS_3d-trig-pythag-m1](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/SyllabAI/syllabai-resources/3b2ce8da700b80f51700fb34fc721c90d6654d6b/SME-ExamQuestion/cie-igcse-maths-international-maths-23-extended/pythagoras-and-trigonometry/3d-pythagoras-and-trigonometry/assets/015-oju1v9fs-3d-trig-pythag-m1.png)

> *We need to find angle **x**. Notice that we have side **AF.** In order to find the required angle we first need to find the length of the side **FH**. To do this draw a right angled triangle connecting hypotenuse **FH** with two sides whose lengths are known.*

![3d-trig-pythag-m1-2](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/SyllabAI/syllabai-resources/3b2ce8da700b80f51700fb34fc721c90d6654d6b/SME-ExamQuestion/cie-igcse-maths-international-maths-23-extended/pythagoras-and-trigonometry/3d-pythagoras-and-trigonometry/assets/016-3d-trig-pythag-m1-2.png)

> *In triangle **EFH **we can use Pythagoras' Theorem to find **FH.*

$FH=\sqrt{9^{2}+5^{2}}$

**[1]**

$=\sqrt{106}$

> *It is best to leave this result in its exact form for accuracy. We can add this result to our diagram.*

![3d-trig-pythag-m1-3](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/SyllabAI/syllabai-resources/3b2ce8da700b80f51700fb34fc721c90d6654d6b/SME-ExamQuestion/cie-igcse-maths-international-maths-23-extended/pythagoras-and-trigonometry/3d-pythagoras-and-trigonometry/assets/017-3d-trig-pythag-m1-3.png)

> *Now we can use right-angle trigonometry to find the required angle.*

$\begin{gathered} \tan ( x ) & = \frac{6}{ \sqrt{106} } \end{gathered}$

**[1]**

> *Use the inverse tangent function ("SHIFT tan" on your calculator) to find **x.*

$\begin{gathered} x = \tan ^{- 1} ( \frac{6}{ \sqrt{106} } ) \end{gathered}$

**[1]**

$\begin{gathered} = 30.23241412... \end{gathered}$

> *Round your answer to 3 significant figures as requested. Remember to include the units.*

**Answer = **$30.2^{\circ}$ **[1]**

The diagram shows a triangular prism.

![q19-paper2h-june2018-edexcel-igcse-maths](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/SyllabAI/syllabai-resources/3b2ce8da700b80f51700fb34fc721c90d6654d6b/SME-ExamQuestion/cie-igcse-maths-international-maths-23-extended/pythagoras-and-trigonometry/3d-pythagoras-and-trigonometry/assets/062-q19-paper2h-june2018-edexcel-igcse-maths.png)

$AF=10\mathrm{cm},AB=24\mathrm{cm}$ and$BC=8\mathrm{cm}$. 
Angle$FAB$ = angle $ADC$ = angle $BCD=90^{\circ}$

Work out the size of the angle between the line $BE$ and the plane $ABCD$. 
Give your answer correct to 1 decimal place.
parts.solutionMd:
> *To find the angle between a line and a plane it is helpful to draw a right angled triangle using the line that is perpendicular to the plane:*

![3d-trig-pythag-h5-1](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/SyllabAI/syllabai-resources/3b2ce8da700b80f51700fb34fc721c90d6654d6b/SME-ExamQuestion/cie-igcse-maths-international-maths-23-extended/pythagoras-and-trigonometry/3d-pythagoras-and-trigonometry/assets/063-3d-trig-pythag-h5-1.png)

> *In order to find the required angle you will first need to find the length of the side **DB**. To do this draw a right angled triangle joining **DB** with two other known sides:*

![3d-trig-pythag-h5-2](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/SyllabAI/syllabai-resources/3b2ce8da700b80f51700fb34fc721c90d6654d6b/SME-ExamQuestion/cie-igcse-maths-international-maths-23-extended/pythagoras-and-trigonometry/3d-pythagoras-and-trigonometry/assets/064-3d-trig-pythag-h5-2.png)

> *Now we can use Pythagoras to find **DB**.*

$\begin{gathered} D B^{2} & = 8^{2} + 24^{2} \\ D B & = \sqrt{8^{2} + 24^{2}} \\ = 8 \sqrt{10} \end{gathered}$

**[1]**

> *Mark this length on the diagram*

![3d-trig-pythag-h5-3](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/SyllabAI/syllabai-resources/3b2ce8da700b80f51700fb34fc721c90d6654d6b/SME-ExamQuestion/cie-igcse-maths-international-maths-23-extended/pythagoras-and-trigonometry/3d-pythagoras-and-trigonometry/assets/065-3d-trig-pythag-h5-3.png)

> *Now we know the opposite and adjacent sides in a right-angle triangle so use the tangent ratio to find the required angle*

$\tan ( x ) = \frac{10}{8 \sqrt{10} }$

**[1]**

> *Find the angle by using the inverse tan function ("SHIFT tan" on your calculator)*

$\begin{gathered} x = \tan ^{- 1} ( \frac{10}{8 \sqrt{10} } ) \\ = 21.5681294... \end{gathered}$

> *Round your answer to 1 decimal place as requested. Remember to include the units*

**Answer = **$21.6^{\circ}$ **[1]**

parts.solutionMd:

> *So put some imaginary lengths into the diagram- it makes sense to use the simplest form of the given ratio!*

![3d-trig-pythag-m3](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/SyllabAI/syllabai-resources/3b2ce8da700b80f51700fb34fc721c90d6654d6b/SME-ExamQuestion/cie-igcse-maths-international-maths-23-extended/pythagoras-and-trigonometry/3d-pythagoras-and-trigonometry/assets/097-3d-trig-pythag-m3.png)

> *We need to find angle **x**. Notice that we have side **CF.** In order to find the required angle we first need to find the length of the side **AC**. To do this draw a right angled triangle connecting hypotenuse **AC** with two sides whose lengths are known:*

![3d-trig-pythag-m3-2](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/SyllabAI/syllabai-resources/3b2ce8da700b80f51700fb34fc721c90d6654d6b/SME-ExamQuestion/cie-igcse-maths-international-maths-23-extended/pythagoras-and-trigonometry/3d-pythagoras-and-trigonometry/assets/099-3d-trig-pythag-m3-2.png)

> *In triangle **ABC** we can use Pythagoras' Theorem to find **AC.*

$AC=\sqrt{4^{2}+2^{2}}$

**[1]**

$=2\sqrt{5}$

> *It is best to leave this result in its exact form for accuracy. We can add this result to our diagram:*

![nIinGUCl_3d-trig-pythag-m3-3](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/SyllabAI/syllabai-resources/3b2ce8da700b80f51700fb34fc721c90d6654d6b/SME-ExamQuestion/cie-igcse-maths-international-maths-23-extended/pythagoras-and-trigonometry/3d-pythagoras-and-trigonometry/assets/100-niingucl-3d-trig-pythag-m3-3.png)

> *Now we can use right-angle trigonometry to find the required angle.*

$\begin{gathered} \tan ( x ) & = \frac{3}{2 \sqrt{5} } \end{gathered}$

**[1]**

$\begin{gathered} x = \tan ^{- 1} ( \frac{3}{2 \sqrt{5} } ) \\ = 33.85451481... \end{gathered}$

parts.problemMd:
The length of a diagonal of a cuboid is 20 cm

The diagonal makes an angle of 24° with the base.

The area of the base is 150 cm<sup>2</sup>

![q24-paper-3h-june-2019-aqa-gcse-maths](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/SyllabAI/syllabai-resources/3b2ce8da700b80f51700fb34fc721c90d6654d6b/SME-ExamQuestion/cie-igcse-maths-international-maths-23-extended/pythagoras-and-trigonometry/3d-pythagoras-and-trigonometry/assets/049-q24-paper-3h-june-2019-aqa-gcse-maths.png)

Work out the volume of the cuboid.

...................................... cm<sup>3</sup>
parts.solutionMd:
*The volume of a cuboid, **V**, is the area of its base, 150 cm*<sup>*2*</sup>*, multiplied by its height, **h* * *

**V*** = 150 × ***h***  *

*Write the 20 cm and** h** on the diagram* * *

![cuboid-h](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/SyllabAI/syllabai-resources/3b2ce8da700b80f51700fb34fc721c90d6654d6b/SME-ExamQuestion/cie-igcse-maths-international-maths-23-extended/pythagoras-and-trigonometry/3d-pythagoras-and-trigonometry/assets/050-cuboid-h.png)

> * *

*The triangle formed with the diagonal is a right-angled triangle, so SOHCAHTOA can be used* *Use sin **x** = *$\frac{\mathrm{opp}}{\mathrm{hyp}}$* * * *

$\mathrm{sin}24=\frac{h}{20}$

**[1]**

*Multiply both sides by 20 to calculate **h* * *

$20\mathrm{sin}24=h$

**[1]**

*Find the volume of the cuboid, by substituting this height into the volume formula above*

$V=150\times20\mathrm{sin}24$

**1220 cm**<sup>**3**</sup> **[1]**

**The question can also be done using** $\mathrm{cos}66=\frac{h}{20}$

**Answers within the range 1215 to 1221 are accepted**

parts.problemMd:
![cie-igcse-2020-oct-nov-p4-tz3-q6a](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/SyllabAI/syllabai-resources/3b2ce8da700b80f51700fb34fc721c90d6654d6b/SME-ExamQuestion/cie-igcse-maths-international-maths-23-extended/pythagoras-and-trigonometry/3d-pythagoras-and-trigonometry/assets/022-cie-igcse-2020-oct-nov-p4-tz3-q6a.png)

*ABCDEFGH* is a cuboid. *AB* = 8 cm, *BC *= 5 cm and *CG* = 11 cm.

i) Calculate angle *CAB*.

Angle* CAB* = ................................................ [2]

ii) Calculate angle *GAC*.

Angle* GAC *= ................................................ [2]
parts.solutionMd:
i) *The angle **CAB **is opposite the side **BC **and adjacent to the side **AB**, so use the tan ratio.  *

$\begin{array}{rcl} \tan C A B & = \frac{B C}{A B} \\ \tan C A B & = \frac{5}{8} \end{array}$

**[1]**

> *Use the tan*<sup>*-1 *</sup>*button on your calculator to find the angle.*

$\begin{gathered} C A B & = \tan ^{- 1} ( \frac{5}{8} ) \\ = 32.0053... \end{gathered}$

**Angle ****CAB ****= 32.0° (1 d.p.) ****[1]**

ii) *The angle **GAC **is opposite the side **CG. **The hypotenuse is the diagonal **AG**, so use the sine ratio. *

> *Use the unrounded version of your answer for **AG **from part (b).  *

$\begin{gathered} \sin G A C & = \frac{G C}{A G} \\ \sin G A C & = \frac{11}{ \sqrt{210} } \end{gathered}$

**[1]**

> *Use the sin*<sup>*-1 *</sup>*button on your calculator to find the angle.  *

$\begin{gathered} G A C & = \sin ^{- 1} ( \frac{11}{ \sqrt{210} } ) \\ = 49.3824... \end{gathered}$

**Angle ****GAC ****= 49.4° (1 d.p.) ****[1]**

The diagram shows a cuboid.
$AB$ = 8 cm, $BC$ = 4 cm and $CR$ = 5 cm.

Calculate the angle between the diagonal $AR$ and the plane $BCRQ$.
parts.solutionMd:
> *The line *$AR$* and the line *$AB$* form a right-angle triangle with the line *$RB$*- which is on the plane *$BCRQ$* as shown below. The angle between the diagonal *$AR$* and the plane *$BCRQ$* is therefore the angle between *$AR$*and the line *$RB$*.*

![Diagram of a rectangular box showing dimensions and marked angles. Points A, B, C, D form base; P, Q, R, S form top. Red lines highlight the required angle.](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/SyllabAI/syllabai-resources/3b2ce8da700b80f51700fb34fc721c90d6654d6b/SME-ExamQuestion/cie-igcse-maths-international-maths-23-extended/pythagoras-and-trigonometry/3d-pythagoras-and-trigonometry/assets/004-diagram-of-a-rectangular-box-showing-dimensions-.png)

**identifying the required angle ****[1]**

> *Angle *$ABR$* is a right angle so to find angle *$ARB$* we can use the tangent ratio with *$AB=8$* and *$BR$*.*

> *To find *$BR$* we can use Pythagoras' theorem with *$CR=5$* and *$BC=4$*.*

$BR=\sqrt{4^{2}+5^{2}}$

**[1]**

> *Now we can apply the tangent ratio to find the angle. *

$\tan ( A R B ) = \frac{8}{ \sqrt{4^{2} + 5^{2}} }$

**[1]**

> *Inverse tangent on your calculator to find the angle.*

$\begin{gathered} A R B & = \tan ^{- 1} ( \frac{8}{ \sqrt{4^{2} + 5^{2}} } ) \\ = 51.32655062...^{\circ} \end{gathered}$

**51.3° ****[1]**
**Give answers in degrees to at least one decimal place**

parts.problemMd:
The diagram shows a right-angled triangular prism ABCDEF.

![q18-paper4-nov2019-ocr-gcse-maths](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/SyllabAI/syllabai-resources/3b2ce8da700b80f51700fb34fc721c90d6654d6b/SME-ExamQuestion/cie-igcse-maths-international-maths-23-extended/pythagoras-and-trigonometry/3d-pythagoras-and-trigonometry/assets/040-q18-paper4-nov2019-ocr-gcse-maths.png)

Length AD = 11 cm, length CD = 10 cm and length CF = 6 cm.

Calculate the exact length of AF.

..................................................... cm
parts.solutionMd:
> *Begin by drawing the diagonal from A to C on the base of the diagram. This forms the right-angled triangle ACD**.*

![ocr-gcse-tq-ma-3dpythagtrig-med-q1-diagram-1](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/SyllabAI/syllabai-resources/3b2ce8da700b80f51700fb34fc721c90d6654d6b/SME-ExamQuestion/cie-igcse-maths-international-maths-23-extended/pythagoras-and-trigonometry/3d-pythagoras-and-trigonometry/assets/041-ocr-gcse-tq-ma-3dpythagtrig-med-q1-diagram-1.png)

> *Use Pythagoras' theorem, *$a^{2}+b^{2}=c^{2}$*, on the right-angled triangle ACD to find the length AC.*

$\begin{gathered} A C^{2 } & = 11^{2} + 10^{2} \end{gathered}$

The diagram shows an open box $ABCDEFGH$ in the shape of a cuboid.

$AB=20$ cm, $BC=18$ cm and $AE=16$ cm.

A thin rod $AGX$ rests partly in the box as shown.

The rod is $40$ cm long.

Calculate $GX$, the length of the rod which is outside the box.

$GX=$ ............................................ cm
parts.solutionMd:
> *We know that *$AX=40$* cm so need to find the length *$AG$*. We can use Pythagoras' theorem for this either using it twice in 2D, or once in 3D.*

> *Method 1** - Using 2D Pythagoras' theorem twice*

![5VQRYxOI_ma-cie-igcse-2020-march-p4-tz2-q8bi](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/SyllabAI/syllabai-resources/3b2ce8da700b80f51700fb34fc721c90d6654d6b/SME-ExamQuestion/cie-igcse-maths-international-maths-23-extended/pythagoras-and-trigonometry/3d-pythagoras-and-trigonometry/assets/012-5vqryxoi-ma-cie-igcse-2020-march-p4-tz2-q8bi.png)

$( A C )^{2} = 20^{2} + 18^{2} = 400 + 324 = 724$

**[1]**

> *There is no need to square root as we will need *$( A C )^{2}$* in the next stage.*

$( A G )^{2} = ( A C )^{2} + 16^{2} = 724 + 256 = 980$

**[1]**

$AG=\sqrt{980}=14\sqrt{5}$

> *Now we can find the length of the rod outside of the box (*$GX$*).*

$GX=40-14\sqrt{5}=8.695048...$

**[1]**

**Final answer:** $GX$**, the length of the rod outside the box is 8.70 cm ****[1]**

> *Method 2** - Using 3D Pythagoras' theorem*

$( A G )^{2} = 20^{2} + 18^{2} + 16^{2}$

**[2]**

$AG=\sqrt{980}=14\sqrt{5}$

**[1]**

$GX=40-14\sqrt{5}=8.695048...$

$GX$*, ***the length of the rod outside the box is 8.70 cm*** ***[1]**

parts.problemMd:
The diagram shows a cuboid $ABCDEFGH$.

![q2-hard-4-12-3d-pythogoras-and-trigonometry-edexcel-gcse-maths](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/SyllabAI/syllabai-resources/3b2ce8da700b80f51700fb34fc721c90d6654d6b/SME-ExamQuestion/cie-igcse-maths-international-maths-23-extended/pythagoras-and-trigonometry/3d-pythagoras-and-trigonometry/assets/070-q2-hard-4-12-3d-pythogoras-and-trigonometry-edex.png)

$AB=7\mathrm{cm},AF=5\mathrm{cm} \mathrm{and}FC=15\mathrm{cm}.$

Calculate the volume of the cuboid.

Give your answer correct to $3$ significant figures.
parts.solutionMd:
> *Use Pythagoras' theorem, *$a^{2}+b^{2}=c^{2}$*, on the right-angled triangle **ABF** to find the length **BF**.*

![4-7-16](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/SyllabAI/syllabai-resources/3b2ce8da700b80f51700fb34fc721c90d6654d6b/SME-ExamQuestion/cie-igcse-maths-international-maths-23-extended/pythagoras-and-trigonometry/3d-pythagoras-and-trigonometry/assets/071-4-7-16.png)

$\begin{array}{rcl} 5^{2} + 7^{2} & = B F^{2} \end{array}$

**[1]**

$\begin{gathered} 74 = B F^{2} \\ B F & = \sqrt{74} \text{cm} \end{gathered}$

> *Use Pythagoras' theorem on the right-angled triangle **BCF** to find the length **BC**.*

![4-7-17](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/SyllabAI/syllabai-resources/3b2ce8da700b80f51700fb34fc721c90d6654d6b/SME-ExamQuestion/cie-igcse-maths-international-maths-23-extended/pythagoras-and-trigonometry/3d-pythagoras-and-trigonometry/assets/072-4-7-17.png)

$\begin{gathered} ( \sqrt{74} )^{2} + B C^{2} & = 15^{2} \\ 74 + B C^{2} & = 225 \\ B C^{2} & = 151 \\ B C & = \sqrt{151} \text{cm} \end{gathered}$

**[1]**

> *Calculate the volume of the cuboid, using the formula: *$V=l\times w\times h$*, where *$l$* is the length, *$w$* is the width and *$h$* is the height of the cuboid.*

$\begin{gathered} V = \sqrt{151} \times 7 \times 5 \end{gathered}$

**[1]**

$\begin{array}{rcl} V = 430.087200... \end{array}$

$430\mathrm{cm}^{3}$* ***[1]**

parts.problemMd:
The diagram shows a pyramid.

![q3a-hard-4-12-3d-pythogoras-and-trigonometry-edexcel-gcse-maths](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/SyllabAI/syllabai-resources/3b2ce8da700b80f51700fb34fc721c90d6654d6b/SME-ExamQuestion/cie-igcse-maths-international-maths-23-extended/pythagoras-and-trigonometry/3d-pythagoras-and-trigonometry/assets/058-q3a-hard-4-12-3d-pythogoras-and-trigonometry-ede.png)

$BCDE$is a square with sides of length 10 cm.

The other faces of the pyramid are equilateral triangles with sides of length 10 cm.

Calculate the volume of the pyramid.

Give your answer in the form $\frac{a}{b}\sqrt{2}\mathrm{cm}^{3}$ where $a$ and $b$ are integers to be found.
parts.solutionMd:
> *You will need to know the perpendicular height of the pyramid. *

> *Let **O** be the centre of the base directly below the vertex **A** of the pyramid. *

> *Let **M** be the mid-point of the edge **BC.**  *

> *Look at the right-angled triangle **BOM** and calculate the length **BO **using Pythagoras' theorem: *$a^{2}+b^{2}=c^{2}$*.*

![-g02m5Yf_4-7-10](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/SyllabAI/syllabai-resources/3b2ce8da700b80f51700fb34fc721c90d6654d6b/SME-ExamQuestion/cie-igcse-maths-international-maths-23-extended/pythagoras-and-trigonometry/3d-pythagoras-and-trigonometry/assets/059-g02m5yf-4-7-10.png)

$\begin{gathered} B M^{2} + O M^{2} & = B O^{2} \\ 5^{2} + 5^{2} & = B O^{2} \end{gathered}$

**[1]**

$\begin{gathered} 50 = B O^{2} \\ \sqrt{50} & = B O \\ B O & = 5 \sqrt{2} \text{cm} \end{gathered}$

> *Using Pythagoras' theorem on the right-angled triangle **AOB**, to calculate the perpendicular height of the pyramid, **AO**.*

![-4Fvxw_D_4-7-11](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/SyllabAI/syllabai-resources/3b2ce8da700b80f51700fb34fc721c90d6654d6b/SME-ExamQuestion/cie-igcse-maths-international-maths-23-extended/pythagoras-and-trigonometry/3d-pythagoras-and-trigonometry/assets/060-4fvxw-d-4-7-11.png)

$\begin{gathered} B O + A O^{2} & = A B^{2} \\ ( 5 \sqrt{2} )^{2} + A O^{2} & = 10^{2} \end{gathered}$

**[1]**

$\begin{gathered} 50 + A O^{2} & = 100 \\ A O^{2} & = 50 \\ A O & = 5 \sqrt{2} \text{cm} \end{gathered}$

> *Calculate the area of the base of the pyramid.*

$\begin{gathered} A = 10 \times 10 \\ = 100 cm^{2} \end{gathered}$

> *Calculate the volume of the square-based pyramid, using the formula: *$V=\frac{1}{3}\times Area of base\times Perpendicular height$*.*

$\begin{gathered} V = 1 \frac{1}{3} \times 100 \times 5 \sqrt{2} \end{gathered}$

**[1]**

$\frac{500}{3}\sqrt{2}\mathrm{cm}^{3}$* ***[1]**

parts.problemMd:
The diagram shows a cuboid.

![Cuboid ABCDEFGH with side AH=4cm and AB=5cm](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/SyllabAI/syllabai-resources/3b2ce8da700b80f51700fb34fc721c90d6654d6b/SME-ExamQuestion/cie-igcse-maths-international-maths-23-extended/pythagoras-and-trigonometry/3d-pythagoras-and-trigonometry/assets/001-cuboid-abcdefgh-with-side-ah-4cm-and-ab-5cm.png)

$\begin{gathered} A B & = 5 \text{cm} \end{gathered}$ and $\begin{gathered} A H & = 4 \text{cm} \end{gathered}$.

The size of the angle between $CH$ and the plane $ABCD$ is $35^{\circ}$

Calculate the volume of the cuboid.

Give your answer correct to $3$ significant figures.
parts.solutionMd:
> *To find the volume, you need to first find the depth of the cuboid; *$BC$* **or equivalent*

> *Identify and label the 35° angle between *$CH$* and the plane *$ABCD$* by drawing the right angled triangle *$AHC$

![Cuboid from question with triangle AHC highlighted. Angle HCA is 35](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/SyllabAI/syllabai-resources/3b2ce8da700b80f51700fb34fc721c90d6654d6b/SME-ExamQuestion/cie-igcse-maths-international-maths-23-extended/pythagoras-and-trigonometry/3d-pythagoras-and-trigonometry/assets/002-cuboid-from-question-with-triangle-ahc-highlight.png)

> *Find the length *$AC$* using the tangent ratio*

$\tan ( 35 ) = \frac{4}{A C}$

**[M1]**

$\begin{array}{rcl} A C & = \frac{4}{\tan ( 35 )} \\ = 5.712592027... \end{array}$

**[A1]**

> *Now we can use Pythagoras' Theorem to find *$BC$*; this is the depth of the cuboid*

$\begin{gathered} 5.712...^{2} & = 5^{2} + B C^{2} \end{gathered}$

**[M1]**

$\begin{gathered} B C & = \sqrt{5.712...^{2} - 5^{2}} \\ = 2.762916515... \end{gathered}$

**[A1]**

> *Find the volume using length × height × depth*

$V=4\times5\times2.762916515...\,V=55.2583302...$

> *Round your answer to 3 significant figures as requested*

**55.3 cm**<sup>**3**</sup>

**[A1]**

> **[exam-tip]**
> An alternate method is to find $CH$ using $\frac{4}{\sin ( 35 )}$ and then use 3D Pythagoras to find the depth. $4^{2} + 5^{2} + ( B C )^{2} = ( C H )^{2}$.

parts.problemMd:
The diagram shows a triangular prism.

![q1-veryhard-4-12-3d-pythogoras-and-trigonometry-edexcel-gcse-maths](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/SyllabAI/syllabai-resources/3b2ce8da700b80f51700fb34fc721c90d6654d6b/SME-ExamQuestion/cie-igcse-maths-international-maths-23-extended/pythagoras-and-trigonometry/3d-pythagoras-and-trigonometry/assets/066-q1-veryhard-4-12-3d-pythogoras-and-trigonometry-.png)

The base, $ABCD$, of the prism is a square of side length 15 cm. Angle $ABE$and angle $CBE$are right angles.

Angle $EAB$= 35°

$M$is the point on $DA$such that

$DM:MA=2:3$

Calculate the size of the angle between $EM$and the base of the prism. Give your answer correct to 1 decimal place.
parts.solutionMd:
> *To find the angle between a line and a plane it is helpful to draw a right angled triangle using the line that is perpendicular to the plane.*

![4-12-edexcel-gcse-vhq1-1](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/SyllabAI/syllabai-resources/3b2ce8da700b80f51700fb34fc721c90d6654d6b/SME-ExamQuestion/cie-igcse-maths-international-maths-23-extended/pythagoras-and-trigonometry/3d-pythagoras-and-trigonometry/assets/067-4-12-edexcel-gcse-vhq1-1.png)

> *In order to find the required angle you will first need to find the lengths of the side **MB **and **BE**. To find **BE** draw a right angled triangle **ABE **using the other information you are given.*

![4-12-edexcel-gcse-vhq1-2](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/SyllabAI/syllabai-resources/3b2ce8da700b80f51700fb34fc721c90d6654d6b/SME-ExamQuestion/cie-igcse-maths-international-maths-23-extended/pythagoras-and-trigonometry/3d-pythagoras-and-trigonometry/assets/068-4-12-edexcel-gcse-vhq1-2.png)

> *In the triangle **ABE** you know an angle and the length of the adjacent side. You want to find the length of the opposite side so use the tan ratio.*

$\tan ( 35 ) = \frac{z}{15}$

**[1]**

> *Multiply both sides by 15. Leave as an exact value.*

$\begin{gathered} z = 15 \times \tan ( 35 ) \\ = 15 \tan ( 35 ) \end{gathered}$

> *To find **MB** draw a right angled triangle **ABM **using the other information you are given.*

![4-12-edexcel-gcse-vhq1-3](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/SyllabAI/syllabai-resources/3b2ce8da700b80f51700fb34fc721c90d6654d6b/SME-ExamQuestion/cie-igcse-maths-international-maths-23-extended/pythagoras-and-trigonometry/3d-pythagoras-and-trigonometry/assets/069-4-12-edexcel-gcse-vhq1-3.png)

> *As **DM** : **MA** = 2 : 3, you know that **MA** is *$\frac{3}{2+3}$* of the length of **DA**.*

$MB=\frac{3}{5}\times15=9\mathrm{cm}$

> *In the triangle **ABM** you know two lengths and want to find the hypotenuse so you can use Pythagoras' theorem.*

$\begin{array}{rcl} M A^{2} + A B^{2} & = M B^{2} \\ 9^{2} + 15^{2} & = y^{2} \\ 306 = y^{2} \end{array}$

> *Take the positive square root of both sides. Leave as an exact answer.*

$y=\sqrt{306}$

**[1]**

> *Now you can use the triangle **MBE**. In this triangle you want to find an angle and you know the lengths of the sides that are opposite and adjacent to the angle so use the tan ratio. Use the exact values for the lengths or use your calculator's memory function.*

$\begin{gathered} \tan ( x ) & = \frac{15 \tan ( 35 )}{ \sqrt{306} } \\ = 0.600423... \end{gathered}$

**[1]**

> *Find the angle by using the inverse tan function.*

$\begin{gathered} x = \tan ^{- 1} ( \frac{15 \tan ( 35 )}{ \sqrt{306} } ) \\ = \tan ^{- 1} ( 0.600423... ) \\ = 30.981574... \end{gathered}$

> *Round your answer to 1 decimal place. Remember to include the units.*

$\mathrm{Angle} \mathrm{between}EM\mathrm{and} \mathrm{the} \mathrm{base}=31.0^{\circ}(1\mathrm{dp})$ **[1]**

parts.solutionMd:

> *Look at the right-angled triangle **AMO**, use Pythagoras' theorem, *$a^{2}+b^{2}=c^{2}$*, to calculate the length **AO**.*

![p8VmM8GE_4-7-13](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/SyllabAI/syllabai-resources/3b2ce8da700b80f51700fb34fc721c90d6654d6b/SME-ExamQuestion/cie-igcse-maths-international-maths-23-extended/pythagoras-and-trigonometry/3d-pythagoras-and-trigonometry/assets/074-p8vmm8ge-4-7-13.png)

![4-7-14](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/SyllabAI/syllabai-resources/3b2ce8da700b80f51700fb34fc721c90d6654d6b/SME-ExamQuestion/cie-igcse-maths-international-maths-23-extended/pythagoras-and-trigonometry/3d-pythagoras-and-trigonometry/assets/075-4-7-14.png)

**[1]**

$\begin{gathered} V O & = 20.19706... \text{cm} \end{gathered}$

![1rt7wH2J_4-7-15](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/SyllabAI/syllabai-resources/3b2ce8da700b80f51700fb34fc721c90d6654d6b/SME-ExamQuestion/cie-igcse-maths-international-maths-23-extended/pythagoras-and-trigonometry/3d-pythagoras-and-trigonometry/assets/076-1rt7wh2j-4-7-15.png)

**[1]**

*Calculate the area of one of the triangular faces, using the formula*: $A=\frac{1}{2}bh$*, where *$b$* is the base of the triangle and *$h$* is the perpendicular height.*

$\begin{gathered} A_{triangle} & = 1 \frac{1}{2} \times 20 \times 22.5... \end{gathered}$

**[1]**

$\begin{gathered} A_{triangle} & = 225.371104... cm^{2 } \end{gathered}$

> *Calculate the total surface area by adding together the area of the square base and four of the triangular faces.*

$\begin{gathered} A_{total} & = 20 \times 20 + 4 \times 225.371104... \\ = 1301.48441... cm^{2} \end{gathered}$

> *Round to 2 significant figures.*

$1300\mathrm{cm}^{2}$* ***[1]**

Calculate the length of $AB$.

Give your answer correct to one decimal place.

..................$\mathrm{cm}$
parts.solutionMd:
> *Start by marking the given information on the diagram:*

![3d-trig-pythag-vh5-1](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/SyllabAI/syllabai-resources/3b2ce8da700b80f51700fb34fc721c90d6654d6b/SME-ExamQuestion/cie-igcse-maths-international-maths-23-extended/pythagoras-and-trigonometry/3d-pythagoras-and-trigonometry/assets/039-3d-trig-pythag-vh5-1.png)

> *We cannot assume that **BC** is 6 cm as we are not told that triangle **ABC **is isosceles. Therefore we need to use trigonometry with triangle **BCE **to find** **BC.*

$\sin ( 40 ) = \frac{B C}{13}$

> *Multiply both sides by 13 to find **BC.*

$B C = 13 \sin ( 40 ) = 8.356238926...$

**[1]**

*Store this result in your calculator to preserve accuracy in future calculations.* *We can use this result with the area of triangle **ABC** to find the angle **ACB.*

$22 = 1 \frac{1}{2} ( 6 ) ( 8.356238926... ) \sin C$

**[1]**

> *Rearrange to find the angle **ACB.*

$\sin C = \frac{22}{1 \frac{1}{2} ( 6 ) ( 8.356238926... )} 
C = \sin ^{- 1} ( \frac{22}{1 \frac{1}{2} ( 6 ) ( 8.356238926... )} )
= 61.35273622...$

**[1]**

> *This is the acute angle, so you can subtract this from 180*<sup>*o*</sup>* to find the obtuse angle*

$180-61.35273622...=118.6472638...$

**[1]**

> *Finally, we can use the cosine rule with triangle **ACB** as we have two sides and an included angle, to find **AC*

$A C^{2} = 6^{2} + 8.356...^{2} - 2 ( 6 ) ( 8.356... ) \cos ( 118.647... )$

**[1]**

> *Evaluate and square root both sides to find **AC**.*

$\begin{array}{rcl} A C & = \sqrt{6^{2} + 8.356...^{2} - 2 ( 6 ) ( 8.356... ) \cos ( 118.647... )} \\ = 12.405647... \end{array}$

> *Round your answer to 1 decimal place as requested.*

**Answer = 12.4 cm** **[1]**

ii) *Consider the diagram, **AEX** is a right-angled triangle where **AE **= 12 cm, **EX** = 6.5 cm.*

![cie-igcse-2020-oct-nov-p4-tz2-q9biii-working](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/SyllabAI/syllabai-resources/3b2ce8da700b80f51700fb34fc721c90d6654d6b/SME-ExamQuestion/cie-igcse-maths-international-maths-23-extended/pythagoras-and-trigonometry/3d-pythagoras-and-trigonometry/assets/021-cie-igcse-2020-oct-nov-p4-tz2-q9biii-working.png)

**[1]**

> *Angle **GAX  **is needed so use the triangle formed by the points **G, A **and **X**. **GX** = **h** = 4.121216... cm.*

> *AX** = 13.64735... cm.*

$\begin{gathered} \tan G A X & = \frac{ G X}{A X} \\ = \frac{ 4.121216...}{13.64735} \\ = 0.301979... \end{gathered}$

> *Use the tan*<sup>*-1*</sup>* button to find the answer.*

parts.solutionMd:
> *Draw the stick on the diagram such that it extends from a bottom corner through the diagonally opposite top corner and out of the crate.  *

> *Let the length of the stick inside the crate be **x **cm, then the length of the stick outside of the crate will be 95 - **x **cm.*

$\begin{gathered} c^{2} & = 2 ( 46^{2} ) \\ = 4232 \\ c & = \sqrt{4232} \\ = 46 \sqrt{2} \text{cm} \end{gathered}$

**[1]**

> *Use Pythagoras' theorem on the right-angled triangle made up of the diagonal at the base, the side with length 55 cm and the diagonal made by the part of the stick inside the crate, **x.*

$\begin{gathered} ( 46 \sqrt{2} )^{2} + 55^{2} & = x^{2} \\ 4232 + 3025 & = x^{2} \\ x^{2} & = 7257 \\ x & = \sqrt{7257} \text{cm} \end{gathered}$

**[1]**

> *Calculate the length of the stick that extends out of the crate by subtracting **x** from the length of the stick.*

$9.81\mathrm{cm}$* ***[1]**

parts.problemMd:

$\frac{5}{3x}\times\frac{9x}{20}$
parts.solutionMd:

*Starting with the numbers, we can see that 3 is a multiple of 9 and 3, and that 5 is a multiple of 5 and 20.*

$\frac{ \begin{gathered} 1 \\ \cancel{5} \end{gathered} }{ \begin{gathered} \cancel{3} \cancel{x} \\ 1 \end{gathered} } \times \frac{ \begin{gathered} 3 \\ \cancel{9} \cancel{x} \end{gathered} }{ \begin{gathered} \cancel{20} \\ 4 \end{gathered} } = \frac{1 \times 3}{1 \times 4} = \frac{3}{4}$

parts.problemMd:
Write as a single fraction in its simplest form.

$\frac{x-5}{3}+\frac{6}{x+2}$
parts.solutionMd:
*Two separate fractions become a single fraction when written over the same lowest common denominator* 
*Find the lowest common denominator of *$3$*and *$( x + 2 )$*(by multiplying these together)*

$3\times(x+2)=3(x+2)$

**[1]**

> *Multiply top and bottom of each fraction by the missing terms needed to create the lowest common denominator*

$\begin{gathered} \frac{( x - 5 ) ( x + 2 )}{3 ( x + 2 )} + \frac{6 \times 3}{3 ( x + 2 )} \\ \frac{( x - 5 ) ( x + 2 )}{3 ( x + 2 )} + \frac{18}{3 ( x + 2 )} \end{gathered}$

> *Add the fractions (by adding numerators and placing over one single denominator)*

$\begin{gathered} \frac{( x - 5 ) ( x + 2 ) + 18}{3 ( x + 2 )} \end{gathered}$

**Correct numerator**** [1]**

> *Simplify the numerator (by expanding and collecting)*

$x^{2}-5x+2x-10+18\,x^{2}-3x+8$

> *Write out the final fraction*

$\frac{x^{2}-3x+8}{3(x+2)}$

> *Check if the numerator can be factorised into the form *$( x + 2 ) (... )$* *
*No, so the fraction is fully simplified*

$\frac{x^{2}-3x+8}{3(x+2)}$ **[1]**

**The denominator can also be left expanded as **$3x+6$

> *We can factorise the numerator using the difference between two squares, *$a^{2} - b^{2} = ( a + b ) ( a - b )$

$\frac{( x + 5 ) ( x - 5 )}{x^{2} - 2 x - 35}$

> *We need to factorise the denominator too.*

> *We can factorise the quadratic *$x^{2}-2x-35$* to *`( x +/- box ) ( x +/- box )`* using the acronym TEAM: times for the end, add for the middle. We are looking for two numbers that times to −35 and add to −2. If in doubt, write out the factor pairs of 35:*

*1 and 35: cannot be added to make 2                     *

*5 and 7: can be added to make 2 as "−7 +5 = −2"*

> *So the factorisation is*

$x^{2} - 2 x - 35 = ( x - 7 ) ( x + 5 )$

**[2]**

**1 mark for two numbers in the brackets that multiply to −35 ****or**** add to −2**

> *Now we can write the expression as*

$\frac{( x + 5 ) ( x - 5 )}{( x - 7 ) ( x + 5 )}$

$( x + 5 )$** ***is a common factor to the numerator and denominator, so cancels.*

$\frac{ \cancel{( x + 5 )} ( x - 5 )}{( x - 7 ) \cancel{( x + 5 )} } = \frac{x - 5}{x - 7}$

$\frac{x-5}{x-7}$ **[1]**

parts.problemMd: Write $\frac{x-8}{x}+\frac{3x}{x+1}$ as a single fraction in its simplest form.
parts.solutionMd:
*We need to add the fractions by finding the lowest common denominator, as we would with numeric fractions.* 
*The lowest common denominator is *$x ( x + 1 )$*. So the numerator and denominator of the left fraction needs to be multiplied by *$\frac{( x + 1 )}{( x + 1 )}$* and the right fraction by *$\frac{x}{x}$*.*

$\begin{gathered} \frac{x - 8}{x} + \frac{3 x}{x + 1} & = \frac{x - 8}{x} \times \frac{x + 1}{x + 1} + \frac{3 x}{x + 1} \times \frac{x}{x} \\ \\ = \frac{( x - 8 ) ( x + 1 )}{x ( x + 1 )} + \frac{( 3 x ) ( x )}{x ( x + 1 )} \end{gathered}$

**common denominator " **$\begin{gathered} x ( x + 1 ) \end{gathered}$**" ****[1]**

> *Now we have two fractions with the same denominator, so we can combine them into one fraction.*

$\begin{gathered} = \frac{( x - 8 ) ( x + 1 ) + ( 3 x ) ( x )}{x ( x + 1 )} \end{gathered}$

** ****fractions combined with correct numerator ****[1]**

> *Expand the brackets and collect like terms in the numerator.*

$\begin{gathered} = \frac{x^{2} - 7 x - 8 + 3 x^{2}}{x ( x + 1 )} \\ \\ = \frac{4 x^{2} - 7 x - 8}{x ( x + 1 )} \end{gathered}$

`equation`** [1]**

$= \frac{5 p ( p - 4 )}{2 p^{2} - 32}$

$= \frac{5 p ( p - 4 )}{2 ( p + 4 ) ( p - 4 )}$

**denominator fully factorised ****[1]**

( - 12 ) + ( - 5 ) = - 17$

$\frac{x+5}{x-12}$ **[1]**

parts.problemMd: Simplify $\frac{2x^{2}+x-15}{ax+3a-2bx-6b}$.
parts.solutionMd:
> *To simplify a fraction you would cancel out common factors. Therefore you need to factorise the numerator and denominator.*

> *Starting with the denominator, factorise the first two terms and the last two terms. **a** is the highest common factor of the first two terms and -2**b** is the highest common factor of the last two terms.*

$a x + 3 a - 2 b x - 6 b = a ( x + 3 ) - 2 b ( x + 3 )$

**[1]**

> *Factorise out *$( x + 3 )$* from the new expression.*

$a ( x + 3 ) - 2 b ( x + 3 ) = ( x + 3 ) ( a - 2 b )$

**[1]**

> *Now factorise the numerator. The trick is to check whether either factor of the denominator is a factor of the numerator.*

$( x + 3 ) ( 2 x - 5 ) = 2 x^{2} - 5 x + 6 x - 15 = 2 x^{2} + x - 15$

**[2]**

> *Write the numerator and denominators in their factorised forms and cancel out the common factor.*

$\frac{ \cancel{( x + 3 )} ( 2 x - 5 )}{ \cancel{( x + 3 )} ( a - 2 b )}$

$\frac{2x-5}{a-2b}$** ****[1]**

parts.problemMd:
A car completes a 200 km journey at an average speed of $x$ km/h. 
The car completes **the return journey** of 200 km at an average speed of $(x+10)$ km/h.

i) Show that the difference between the time taken for each of the two journeys is  $\frac{2000}{x(x+10)}$ hours.

[3]

ii) Find the difference between the time taken for each of the two journeys when $x=80$. Give your answer in **minutes **and **seconds**.

................... min .................. s  [3]
parts.solutionMd:
i) *Use the information given to form an equation for the both parts of the journey.*

> *The formula for speed is *$s=\frac{d}{t}$*. *

> *For the first part of the journey, distance = 200 km, speed = *$x$*, let time = *$t.$*   *

$\begin{gathered} x & = \frac{200}{t} ( 1 ) \end{gathered}$**      **

> *For the second part of the journey, distance = 200 km, speed = *$x+10$* , let time = *$T.$*    *

> $\begin{gathered} x + 10 & = \frac{200}{T} ( 2 ) \end{gathered}$*     *

> *Rearrange both equations to make the time the subject.   *

$( 1 ) t = \frac{ 200}{x} 
( 2 ) T = \frac{ 200 }{x + 10}$

** ****Either correct**** [1]*** *

> *Find the difference between the times by subtracting the time for the second journey from the first.  *

> *  *$t-T=\frac{200}{x}-\frac{200}{x+10}$

**[1]***  *

> *Find the common denominator by multiplying them together and change the numerators by multiplying each numerator by the other denominator.   *

$\frac{ 200 ( x + 10 )}{x ( x + 10 )} - \frac{ 200 x}{x ( x + 10 )}$** ***  *

*Find the difference by subtracting only the numerators.***   **

$\frac{ 200 ( x + 10 ) - 200 x}{x ( x + 10 )}$**   **

> *Expand the brackets and simplify the numerator.  *

$\frac{200x+2000-200x}{x(x+10)}=\frac{2000}{x(x+10)}$** ****[1] **

ii) *Substitute *$x=80$* into the expression found in part (i).  *

$\begin{gathered} T - t = \frac{ 2000}{80 ( 80 + 10 )} \end{gathered}$

**[1]*** ***      **

> *Use your calculator to find the value of *$T-t$*.   *

> $\begin{gathered} T - t & = \frac{5}{18} \text{hours} \end{gathered}$* *

**[1]***  *

> *Convert *$\begin{array}{rcl} \frac{5}{18} \end{array}$* hours into minutes by multiplying by 60.   *

`| 5 / 18 x 60 | = 50 / 3 minutes | | _ = 16.66666... minutes | | _ = 16 minutes and 0.6666... minutes | |`

> *Convert 0.666666... minutes into seconds by multiplying by 60. *

*  *$0.66666...\times60=40\mathrm{seconds}$    *  *

$16\mathrm{min}40s$* ***[1]*** *

parts.problemMd:

$8 - 3 x = \frac{( 8 - 3 x ) ( x + 1 )}{x + 1}$

> *Now we can add the fractions.*

$\frac{( 8 - 3 x ) ( x + 1 )}{x + 1} + \frac{10}{x + 1} = \frac{( 8 - 3 x ) ( x + 1 ) + 10}{x + 1}$

**[1]**

> *Expand the brackets in the numerator.*

$=\frac{8x+8-3x^{2}-3x+10}{x+1}$

**[1]**

> *Collect like terms in the numerator.*

**Answer**$=\frac{-3x^{2}+5x+18}{x+1}$** [1]**

parts.problemMd:
$2-\frac{x+2}{x-3}-\frac{x-6}{x+3}$ can be written as a single fraction in the form  $\frac{ax+b}{x^{2}-9}$ where* a* and *b* are integers.

Work out the value of* a* and the value of *b*.
parts.solutionMd:
*Think of 2 as the fraction *$\frac{2}{1}$

$\frac{2}{1}-\frac{x+2}{x-3}-\frac{x-6}{x+3}$

*Find the lowest common denominator of 1, (**x** - 3) and (**x** + 3) by multiplying them together* * *

*lowest common denominator is *$( x - 3 ) ( x + 3 )$

**[1]**

*Multiply top-and-bottom of each fraction by the brackets needed to form this denominator* * *

$\frac{2 ( x - 3 ) ( x + 3 )}{( x - 3 ) ( x + 3 )} - \frac{( x + 2 ) ( x + 3 )}{( x - 3 ) ( x + 3 )} - \frac{( x - 3 ) ( x - 6 )}{( x - 3 ) ( x + 3 )}$ * *

*Write as one single fraction over the common denominator Subtract the numerators* * *

$\frac{2 ( x - 3 ) ( x + 3 ) - ( x + 2 ) ( x + 3 ) - ( x - 3 ) ( x - 6 )}{( x - 3 ) ( x + 3 )}$

**[1]**

*Expand the brackets in the numerator (keeping their results in brackets)* * *

$\frac{2 ( x^{2} - 9 ) - ( x^{2} + 5 x + 6 ) - ( x^{2} - 9 x + 18 )}{( x - 3 ) ( x + 3 )}$

> * *

*Expand the next layer of brackets (being careful to multiply all terms by -1 in the second and third brackets)* * *

$\frac{2 x^{2} - 18 - x^{2} - 5 x - 6 - x^{2} + 9 x - 18}{( x - 3 ) ( x + 3 )}$ * *

> *Collect "like" terms in the numerator  *

$\frac{4 x - 42}{( x - 3 ) ( x + 3 )}$

**[1]**

> *This is not yet in the form *$\frac{ax+b}{x^{2}-9}$*  *
*Expand the brackets in the denominator   *

> $\frac{4x-42}{x^{2}-9}$*  *

> *This is now in the form *$\frac{ax+b}{x^{2}-9}$* where **a **and **b** are integers (whole numbers)  *

**a*** = 4 and ***b*** = - 42*

$\frac{4x-42}{x^{2}-9}$** ****where ****a**** = 4 and ****b**** = - 42 ****[1]**

parts.problemMd: Show that  $\frac{1}{6x^{2}+7x-5}\div\frac{1}{4x^{2}-1}$  simplifies to  $\frac{ax+b}{cx+d}$ where *a, b, c* and *d* are integers.
parts.solutionMd:
*Dividing by *$\frac{a}{b}$* is the same as multiplying by *$\frac{b}{a}$ 
*Flip the second fraction and change ÷ into ×* * *

$\frac{1}{6x^{2}+7x-5}\times\frac{4x^{2}-1}{1}$ * *

*"Simplify" for algebraic fractions means factorise and cancel* *Factorise the numerator of the second fraction using the "difference of two squares" **a*<sup>*2*</sup>* - **b*<sup>*2*</sup>* = (**a **+ **b**)(**a **- **b**)   *

$\begin{gathered} 4 x^{2} - 1 & = ( 2 x )^{2} - 1^{2} \\ = ( 2 x + 1 ) ( 2 x - 1 ) \end{gathered}$

**[1]*** *

*The calculation is now*

$\frac{1}{6 x^{2} + 7 x - 5} \times \frac{( 2 x + 1 ) ( 2 x - 1 )}{1}$

*The harder quadratic on the denominator is likely to have (2**x** + 1) or (2**x** - 1) as a factor* 
*Try factorising with (2**x** + 1)* * *

$6 x^{2} + 7 x - 5 = ( 3 x \pm... ) ( 2 x + 1 ) ?$ * *

*The whole number -5 in the first bracket would multiply by +1 in the second bracket to give -5 on the left *
*But expanding this attempt gives an incorrect middle term* * *

> `( 3 x - 5 ) ( 2 x + 1 ) = 6 x ^2 bottom - 7 x - 5`*  *

*Try factorising with (2**x** - 1)* * *

$6 x^{2} + 7 x - 5 = ( 3 x \pm... ) ( 2 x - 1 ) ?$ * *

*The whole number +5 in the first bracket would multiply by -1 in the second bracket to give -5 on the left *
*Expanding this attempt shows it is correct* * *

$( 3 x + 5 ) ( 2 x - 1 ) = 6 x^{2} + 7 x - 5$

`cbrt( y ^2 ) = sqrt index 6 of x` and `space y equals n-th root of x`.

parts.solutionMd:
> *Method 1*

> *Rewrite the first equation by cubing both sides.*

`y ^2 = ( sqrt index 6 of x ) ^3`

> *Simplify the right hand side by using the index law *$\sqrt[n]{a^{m}} = a ^{\frac{m}{n}} .$* Simplify the fraction.*

$y^{2}=x^{\frac{3}{6}}=x^{\frac{1}{2}}$

$y^{2} = ( \sqrt[n]{x} )^{2}$

$y^{2}=x^{\frac{2}{n}}$

> *The left hand side of both equations are the same. So the right hand sides must also be the same.*

$x^{\frac{1}{2}}=x^{\frac{2}{n}}$

> *The bases are equal so the exponents must also be equal.*

$\frac{1}{2}=\frac{2}{n}$

> *Use equivalent fraction to write both sides with the same numerator.*

$\frac{2}{4}=\frac{2}{n}$

> *The numerators are equal so the denominators must also be equal.*

$n=4$ **[1]**

> *Method 2*

> *Rewrite both equations using indices using the fact *$\sqrt[n]{a^{m}} = a ^{\frac{m}{n}} .$

$y^{\frac{2}{3}}=x^{\frac{1}{6}}\mathrm{and}y=x^{\frac{1}{n}}$

**[1]**

> *Substitute *$y=x^{\frac{1}{n}}$* into *$y^{\frac{2}{3}}=x^{\frac{1}{6}}.$* Use bracket when substituting.*

$( x^{ \frac{1}{n} } )^{ \frac{2}{3} } = x^{ \frac{1}{6} }$

> *Simplify the left hand side by using the index law: *$( a^{m )^{n} = a^{m} \times n} .$

$x^{\frac{2}{3n}}=x^{\frac{1}{6}}$

> *As the bases of both sides are equal then the exponents (indices) of both sides must also be equal.*

$\frac{2}{3n}=\frac{1}{6}$

> *Get rid of the fractions by multiplying both sides by both of the denominators.*

$\begin{gathered} \frac{2}{3 \cancel{n} } \times 3 \cancel{n} \times 6 & = \frac{1}{ \cancel{6} } \times 3 n \times \cancel{6} \\ 12 = 3 n \end{gathered}$

> *Divide both sides by 3.*

$n=4$ **[1]**

> *Divide both sides by *$x^{-2}$*.*

$\frac{x^{-\frac{1}{3}}}{x^{-2}}=32$

**[1]**

> *Simplify the left hand side using the laws of indices. *

> *The base numbers are the same and one term is divided by the other so you can subtract the powers.*

$\begin{gathered} x^{( - 1 \frac{1}{3} - - 2 )} & = 32 \\ x^{ \frac{5}{3} } & = 32 \end{gathered}$

**[1]**

> *Cube both sides.*

$x^{5}=32^{3}\,x^{5}=32768$

> *Find the fifth root of both sides.*

`x equals fifth root of 32768`

$x=8$** [1]**

> *Write out the final answer*

**two of the three final terms correct**** [1]**

$\begin{gathered} ( 3 x - 5 y ) ( 2 x + y ) & = 3 x \times 2 x + 3 x \times y + ( - 5 y ) \times 2 x + ( - 5 y ) \times y \\ = 6 x^{2} + 3 x y - 10 x y - 5 y^{2} \end{gathered}$

**3 correct terms**** [1]**

> *Now simplify by collecting like terms; *$3xy$* and *$-10xy$* are like terms.*

$( 2 x - 5 y ) ( 2 x + y ) = 6 x^{2} - 7 x y - 5 y^{2}$

$6x^{2}-7xy-5y^{2}$* ***[1]**

parts.problemMd: Factorise  $5m^{2}-20p^{4}$.
parts.solutionMd:
*"Factorise" means put into brackets*

*Take out a common factor of 5* * *

$5 m^{2} - 20 p^{4} = 5 ( m^{2} - 4 p^{4} )$

**[1]**

*The "difference of two squares" is *$a^{2} - b^{2} = ( a + b ) ( a - b )$

*Use the difference of two squares to factorise *$m^{2}-4p^{4}$* (*$a=m$* and *$b=2p^{2}$*)* * *

$m^{2} - 4 p^{4} = ( m + 2 p^{2} ) ( m - 2 p^{2} )$

**[1]**

*Put this back into the question* * *

$5 m^{2} - 20 p^{4} = 5 ( m + 2 p^{2} ) ( m - 2 p^{2} )$

$5(m+2p^{2})(m-2p^{2})$** ****[1]**

*"Factorise" means to put into brackets by taking out common numbers and letters*

*Find the biggest number that goes into both 12 and 18* * *

*biggest number is 6* * *

*Find the biggest power of *$a$* that goes into both *$a$* and *$a^{3}$ * *

*biggest power is *$a$ * *

*Find the biggest power of *$b$* that goes into both *$b^{3}$* and *$b^{2}$ * *

*biggest power is *$b^{2}$

*Multiply these together to get the biggest factor that can be taken out * * *

* *$6\times a\times b^{2}=6ab^{2}$ * *

*Write *$6ab^{2}$* outside brackets and write two terms inside the brackets that, if expanded, give *$12ab^{3}+18a^{3}b^{2}$

$6 a b^{2} ( 2 b + 3 a^{2} )$

**Any correct partial factorisation**** [1]**
 $6ab^{2}(2b+3a^{2})$** ****[1]**

i) *The two terms on the left have a common factor of *$m$*, so factorise *$m$* out*

$m(2n+m)-6n-3m$

> *The two terms on the right have a common factor of 3. Notice that both these two terms are negative so the common factor is actually "-3"*

$m(2n+m)-3(2n+m)$

**[1]**

> *Now we can see that *$(2n+m)$* occurs twice. We can use the distributive rule to factorise the entire expression to its final form*

$(m-3)(2n+m)$**  ****[1]**

ii) *Both terms are square, so we need to recognise that this is an example the difference of two squares. *

> *General rule: *$a^{2}-b^{2}=(a+b)(a-b)$* *

> *Find the square root of *$4y^{2}$* and the square root of 81. Hence*

$4y^{2}-81=(2y+9)(2y-9)$

$(2y+9)(2y-9)$ **[1]**

iii) *When factorising quadratics like this, it's helpful to remember "TEAM": **T**imes for the **E**nd, **A**dd for the **M**iddle. *

> *So we're looking for two integers that will times to +8 and add to -6, to go into the blank spaces below*

`t ^2 - 6 t + 8 = ( t + box _ ) ( t + box _ )`

> *Factors of 8 are;         1 and 8      can't sum to -6*

> *                  2 and 4      can sum to -6 if  -2 and -4*

> *So the numbers in the blank spaces are -2 and -4*

`t ^2 - 6 t + 8 = ( t + box - 2 ) ( t + box - 4 )`

$(t-2)(t-4)$

**two numbers in the brackets that multiply to -6 [****1]**

**two numbers in the brackets that sum to 8**** ****[****1]**

parts.problemMd:
Expand and simplify.

$( x - 2 ) ( x + 5 ) ( 2 x - 1 )$
parts.solutionMd:
> *Expand the first two brackets by multiplying everything in the first bracket by everything in the second bracket.*

$\begin{gathered} ( x - 2 ) ( x + 5 ) \\ = x ( x + 5 ) - 2 ( x + 5 ) \\ = x^{2} + 5 x - 2 x - 10 \end{gathered}$

**[1]**

> *Simplify this. *

$\begin{gathered} x^{2} + 5 x - 2 x - 10 & = x^{2} + 3 x - 10 \end{gathered}$

> *Write the expanded expression out next to the third bracket. *

$\begin{gathered} ( x^{2} + 3 x - 10 ) ( 2 x - 1 ) \end{gathered}$

> *Multiply each part of the first bracket by *$( 2 x - 1 )$*. *

$\begin{gathered} x^{2} ( 2 x - 1 ) + 3 x ( 2 x - 1 ) - 10 ( 2 x - 1 ) \end{gathered}$

> *Expand the brackets. *

$\begin{gathered} 2 x^{3} - x^{2} + 6 x^{2} - 3 x - 20 x - ( - 10 ) \end{gathered}$

**[1]**

> *Simplify. *

$\begin{array}{c} 2 x^{ } 3 + 5 x^{ } 2 - 23 x + 10\end{array}$**[1]**

parts.problemMd: Write $( x + 1 ) ( x - 3 )^{2}$ in the form $ax^{3}+bx^{2}+cx+d$.
parts.solutionMd:
> *Rewrite the equation with the squared brackets as two separate brackets.*

> $( x + 1 ) ( x - 3 ) ( x - 3 )$*  *

> *Expand the first two brackets by multiplying everything in the first bracket by everything in the second bracket.*

$\begin{gathered} ( x + 1 ) ( x - 3 ) \\ = x ( x - 3 ) + 1 ( x - 3 ) \\ = x^{2} - 3 x + 1 x - 3 \end{gathered}$

**[1]**

> *Simplify this. *

$\begin{gathered} x^{2} - 3 x + 1 x - 3 & = x^{2} - 2 x - 3 \end{gathered}$

> *Write the expanded expression out next to the third bracket. *

$\begin{gathered} ( \begin{gathered} x^{2} - 2 x - 3 \end{gathered} ) ( x - 3 ) \end{gathered}$

> *Multiply each part of the first bracket by *$( x - 3 )$*. *

$\begin{gathered} x^{2} ( x - 3 ) - 2 x ( x - 3 ) - 3 ( x - 3 ) \end{gathered}$

> *Expand the brackets, taking extra care with the negatives. *

$\begin{gathered} x^{3} - 3 x^{2} - 2 x^{2} + 6 x - 3 x - ( - 9 ) \end{gathered}$

**[1]**

> *Simplify, taking extra care with the negatives. *

$\begin{array}{c} x^{ } 3 - 5 x^{ } 2 + 3 x + 9\end{array}$**[1] **
**This could be done by expanding (****x**** -3)**<sup>**2 **</sup>**first.**

parts.problemMd:
Expand and simplify.

$(y+3)(y-4)(2y-1)$
parts.solutionMd:
> *First expand the first pair of brackets.*

$( y + 3 ) ( y - 4 ) ( 2 y - 1 ) = ( y^{2} - y - 12 ) ( 2 y - 1 )$

**[1]**

> *Carefully expand, using separate lines to make sure all terms are included and lining like terms up so simplifying is easy.*

$\begin{gathered} ( y^{2} - y - 12 ) ( 2 y - 1 ) & = 2 y^{3} - y^{2} \\ - 2 y^{2} + y \\ - 24 y + 12 \end{gathered}$

**[1]**

> *Simplify.*

$2y^{3}-y^{2}-2y^{2}+y-24y+12=2y^{3}-3y^{2}-23y+12$

$2y^{3}-3y^{2}-23y+12$** ****[1]**

parts.problemMd:
Factorise completely.

i) $15p^{2}q^{2}-25q^{3}$

[2]

ii) $4fg+6gh+10fk+15hk$

[2]

iii) $81k^{2}-m^{2}$

[2]
parts.solutionMd:
> *Factorise **completely **means we must factorise using the highest common factor, e.g. *$5x^{3}+10x^{2}$* would factorise to *$5 x^{2} ( x + 2 )$* rather than just *$x ( 5 x^{2} + 10 x )$

i) *The highest common factor of these two terms is *$5q^{2}$

**Correct factorisation, but not using highest common factor**** [1]**

$5q^{2}(3p^{2}-5q)$ **[1]** 
**It is worth expanding your answer to check**

ii) *The first two terms have a highest common factor of *$2g$*, so this can be factored out*

$2 g ( 2 f + 3 h ) + 10 f k + 15 h k$

> *The second two terms have a highest common factor of *$5k$*, so this can be factored out*

$2 g ( 2 f + 3 h ) + 5 k ( 2 f + 3 h )$

**[1]**

> *These two terms have a common factor of *$( 2 f + 3 h )$* so this can be factored out*

$(2f+3h)(2g+5k)$ **[1] **
**It is worth expanding your answer to check**

iii) *This is a "difference of two squares pattern" as it is in the form of "something squared" subtract "something else squared" *

> *e.g. *$x^{2} - 9 = ( x + 3 ) ( x - 3 )$* or *$( a^{2} - b^{2} ) = ( a + b ) ( a - b )$

> *Rewrite as *$( a^{2} - b^{2} )$

$( 81 k^{2} - m^{2} ) = ( ( 9 k )^{2} - ( m )^{2} )$

> *Use the pattern of difference of two squares*

$(9k+m)(9k-m)$ **[2] **
**It is worth expanding your answer to check**

parts.problemMd: Factorise  $3x^{2}+11x--20$
parts.solutionMd:
*Multiply 3 by -20 (the first and last numbers)*

*3 × -20 = -60*

*Find two numbers that multiply to give -60 and add to give 11 (the middle number)*

*15 and -4*

*Split the middle term into 15**x** and -4**x*

$3x^{2}+15x-4x-20$

*Factorise fully the first pair of terms and the second pair of terms *

$3 x ( x + 5 ) - 4 ( x + 5 )$

**or x(3x - 4) + 5(3x - 4) if terms written other way round**** [1] **

*Factorise out the whole (x + 5) bracket as if it were one term, leaving 3**x** and -4 in their own bracket*

$( x + 5 ) ( 3 x - 4 )$

$(x+5)(3x-4)$ **[1]**

parts.problemMd:
Factorise completely.

$2t^{2}-98m^{2}$
parts.solutionMd:
*"Factorise" means write as brackets to be expanded* *Take out a common factor of 2* * *

$2 t^{2} - 98 m^{2} = 2 ( t^{2} - 49 m^{2} )$

**[1]**

*The "difference of two squares" says  *$a^{2} - b^{2} = ( a + b ) ( a - b )$

*Use the difference of two squares to factorise *$t^{2}-49m^{2}$* (using *$a=t$* and *$b=7m$*)* * *

$t^{2} - 49 m^{2} = ( t + 7 m ) ( t - 7 m )$

**[1]**

*Write the final answer out* * *

$2 t^{2} - 98 m^{2} = 2 ( t + 7 m ) ( t - 7 m )$

$2(t+7m)(t-7m)$* ***[1]** 
**Final answers such as **$( 2 t + 14 m ) ( t - 7 m )$** are not factorised completely**

parts.problemMd: Find the value of $\mathrm{log}_{2}16$
parts.solutionMd:
> *Rewrite using the definition of logarithms: If *$log_{a} ( b ) = x$* then *$a^{x}=b$

$2^{x}=16$

> *Rewrite 16 as a power of 2*

$2^{x}=2^{4}$

> *As the bases are equal, the powers are also equal*

$\mathrm{log}_{2}16=4$** ****[1]**

> *If *$a^{x}=b$* then *$log_{a} ( b ) = x$

$a=10$

$x=\mathrm{log}_{10}y$** also accepted**

> *If no base is shown then use log to the base ten*

$\begin{gathered} log_{10} ( 2 x ) & = 5 \\ a = 10 \\ b = 2 x \\ \\ 2 x & = 10^{5} \end{gathered}$

**[1]**

> *Rearrange to find *$x$

$x=\frac{10^{5}}{2}=\frac{100000}{2}$* *

$x=50000$**[1]**

parts.problemMd:
Rangan buys 3.6kg of potatoes and 2.8kg of leeks.

The total cost is \$13.72.

Leeks cost \$2.65 per kilogram.

Find the cost of 1 kg of potatoes.

\$ ................................................
parts.solutionMd:

$2.8\times2.65=7.42$* *

**[1]**

> *Let 1kg of potatoes be **p.*

> *Form an equation in terms of **p.*

$3.6p+7.42=13.72$

> *Subtract the cost of the leeks from the total cost of Rangan's shopping.*

$3.6p=13.72-7.42\,3.6p=6.3$* *

> *So the total cost of the potatoes was \$6.30.*

**[1]**

> *Remember to write the final answer in \$ correct to 2 decimal places.*

**\$1.75 ****[1]**

parts.problemMd:
Ahmed sells different types of cake in his shop. 
The cost of each cake depends on its type and its size.

Every small cake costs `$ x` and every large cake costs $\$ ( 2 x + 1 )$The total cost of 3 small lemon cakes and 2 large lemon cakes is \$12.36.

Find the cost of a small lemon cake.

\$ ................................................
parts.solutionMd:
> *Let one small lemon cake be *$x$* and one large lemon cake be *$2x+1$*. *
*Form an equation in terms of *$x.$

$3 x + 2 ( 2 x + 1 ) = 12.36$

**[1]**

$3x+4x+2=12.36$

> *Simplify.*

$7x+2=12.36$

**[1]**

> $x=1.48$* so one small lemon cake = \$1.48.*

parts.problemMd:
The angles of a quadrilateral are $x^{\circ}$, $(x+5)^{\circ}$, $(2x-25)^{\circ}$ and $(x+10)^{\circ}$.

Find the value of $x$.

$x$ = ...................................................
parts.solutionMd:
*Angles in a quadrilateral add up to 360*<sup>*o*</sup>*.* 
*Write down an equation adding together all four angles.*

$x+(x+5)+(2x-25)+(x+10)=360$

> *You can re-write the equation without brackets.*

$x+x+5+2x-25+x+10=360$

**[1]**

> *Re-arrange the equation so that like terms are next to each other, remember to keep the sign in front of each term the same as it was when you re-arrange. *

$x+x+2x+x+5-25+10=360$

> *Add/subtract the like terms, being careful with negatives!*

$5x-10=360$

**[1]**

> *Add 10 to both sides.*

parts.solutionMd:
i) *We can start by writing*

`y ^2 + 5 y - 84 = ( y box ) ( y box )`

> *To work out the missing numbers in the brackets, we are looking for two numbers that multiply to −84 and add to 5. (The acronym TEAM may help you to remember what to do: **T**imes for the **E**nd, **A**dd for the **M**iddle)*

> *If the two numbers are not obvious, use your calculator to help you write down factor pairs of −84:*

*1 and 84*

*2 and 41*

*3 and 28*

*4 and 21*

*6 and 14*

*7 and 12*

> *7 and 12 is the first pair that can be added or subtracted to make 5. *

*12 − 7 = 5    and    12 × (−7) = −84*

> *So the missing numbers in the brackets are +12 and −7.*

$y^{2} + 5 y - 84 = ( y + 12 ) ( y - 7 )$

$(y+12)(y-7)$** **
**two numbers in the brackets that multiply to −84 ****[1] **
**two numbers in the brackets that add to 5 ****[1]**

ii) *Area of rectangle = length × width. Substitute into this formula, length = *$y+5$*, width = *$y$*, and area = 84. *

$( y + 5 ) \times y = 84$

**[1]**

> *Expand*

$y ( y + 5 ) = 84
y^{2} + 5 y = 84$

> *Rearrange to a quadratic equation in the form from part (b)(i) and factorise using the answer of part (b)(i)*

$y^{2} + 5 y - 84 = 0
( y + 12 ) ( y - 7 ) = 0$

> *We can solve using the rule that if **A**×**B** = 0, then either **A **= 0 or **B** = 0.*

$y+12=0\mathrm{or}y-7=0\,y=-12\mathrm{or}y=7$

**[1]**

> *Clearly the length of a rectangle cannot be a negative number so we should ignore *$y=-12$* and only use *$y=7$*. *
*Be careful to answer the question- which asks for the perimeter of the rectangle, not simply *$y$*! *
*Perimeter = *$2 ( y + 5 ) + 2 y$*. Substitute in *$y=7$*.*

*Perimeter *$= 2 ( 7 + 5 ) + 2 ( 7 ) = 38$

**38  cm*** ***[1]**

parts.solutionMd:
> *Method 1*

*Angles in a quadrilateral add up to 360*<sup>*o*</sup>*.* 
*Write down an equation adding together all four angles.*

$2x+2x+(3x-15)+(2x+24)=360$

> *You can rewrite the equation without brackets.*

$2x+2x+3x-15+2x+24=360$

**[1]**

> *Rearrange the equation so that like terms are next to each other, remember to keep the sign in front of each term the same as it was when you re-arrange. *

$2x+2x+3x+2x-15+24=360$

> *Add/subtract the like terms, being careful with negatives!*

$9x+9=360$

**[1]**

> *Solve the equation. It may be easiest to factorise the 9 out first.*

$\begin{gathered} 9 x + 9 & = 360 \\ 9 ( x + 1 ) & = 360 \\ x + 1 & = \frac{ 360}{9} \\ x + 1 & = 40 \\ x & = 39 \end{gathered}$

$x=39^{\circ}$ **[1]**

> *Method 2*

> *Opposite angles in a parallelogram are equal.*

> *Write down an equation for the two opposite angles that have **different **expressions.*

$3x-15=2x+24$

**[1]**

> *Solve the equation by first bringing the **x** terms to one side.  *
*The easiest method is to subtract the **x** term with the smallest coefficient.*

$\begin{gathered} 3 x - 15 & = 2 x + 24 \\ - 2 x & = - 2 x \\ x - 15 & = 24 \end{gathered}$

> *Add 15 to both sides.*

$\begin{gathered} x - 15 & = 24 \\ + 15 & = + 15 \\ x & = 39 \end{gathered}$

**[1]**

$x=39^{\circ}$ **[1]**

parts.solutionMd:
i) *Use the information given to form an equation for the perimeter and an equation for the area of the rectangle. *

$( 1 ) l = 40 - x
( 2 ) A = x ( 40 - x )$

**[1]**

$A=40x-x^{2}$

ii) *Substitute *$A=300$* into the equation from part (i).   *

- 30 + ( - 10 ) = - 40$*  *

> * *

> $\begin{gathered} x^{2 } - 40 x + 200 & = 0 \end{gathered}$*     *

> *The quadratic formula for an equation in the form *$ax^{2}+bx+c=0$*  is  *$x=\frac{-b\pm\sqrt{b^{2}-4ac}}{2a}.$

$x = \frac{- ( - 40 ) \pm \sqrt{( - 40 )^{2 } - 4 ( 1 ) ( 200 )} }{2 ( 1 )}$

**Correct use of the formula****  [1]**

**   ***Simplify.*

$\begin{gathered} x & = \frac{40 \pm \sqrt{800} }{2} \\ = \frac{40 \pm 20 \sqrt{2} }{2} \\ = 20 \pm 10 \sqrt{2} \end{gathered}$

*Find both answers. *

> *   *$\begin{gathered} x & = 20 + 10 \sqrt{2} \\ = 34.142135... \end{gathered}$*   *

> *or,*

$\begin{gathered} x & = 20 - 10 \sqrt{2} \\ = 5.857864... \end{gathered}$

> *     *

$x=34.14\mathrm{cm} \mathrm{or}x=5.86\mathrm{cm}(2d.p.)$

Solve this equation to find the cost of a small coffee cake. 
Show all your working.

parts.solutionMd:

> *Form an equation in terms of *$x$* for the number, *$a$*, of small coffee cakes that can be bought for \$20*

$\begin{gathered} a x & = 20 \\ a & = \frac{20}{x} \end{gathered}$

> *Form an equation in terms of *$x$* for the number, *$b$*, of large coffee cakes that can be bought for \$10*

$\begin{gathered} b ( 2 x + 1 ) & = 10 \\ b & = \frac{10}{2 x + 1} \end{gathered}$

**Correct expression for a or b ****[1]**

> *Substitute the expressions for *$a$* and *$b$* into the equation for the total number of cakes*

$\begin{array}{rcl} a + b & = 45 \\ ( \frac{20}{x} ) + ( \frac{10}{2 x + 1} ) & = 45 \end{array}$

parts.solutionMd:
i) *Substitute the values into the formula for compound interest.*

*Formula for compound interest *$A = P ( 1 + \frac{r}{100} )^{n}$*.*

*A** = final amount = 206.46*

*P  =** initial amount = 200*

*r**  =  interest rate = **r*

> *n** = number of years = 2.*

**[1]**

> *   Divide both sides by 200.  *

$( 1 + \frac{r}{100} )^{2} = \frac{206.46}{200} 
( 1 + \frac{r}{100} )^{2} = 1.0323$

> *     Expand the brackets by multiplying every term in the first bracket by every term in the second bracket.   *

$\begin{gathered} ( 1 + \frac{r}{100} ) ( 1 + \frac{r}{100} ) & = 1.0323 \\ 1 ( 1 + \frac{r}{100} ) + \frac{r}{100} ( 1 + \frac{r}{100} ) & = 1.0323 \\ 1 + \frac{r}{100} + \frac{r}{100} + ( \frac{r}{100} )^{2} & = 1.0323 \\ 1 + \frac{2 r}{100} + ( \frac{r}{100} )^{2} & = 1.0323 \end{gathered}$

**[1]**

> *    Set equal to zero and rearrange. *

> *      *

$\begin{gathered} 1 + \frac{2 r}{100} + ( \frac{r}{100} )^{2} - 1.0323 & = 0 \\ ( \frac{r}{100} )^{2} + \frac{2 r}{100} - 0.0323 & = 0 \end{gathered}$

> *    *

> *     Remove the fractions by multiplying every term by 100*<sup>*2*</sup>* .*

> *  *

$\begin{gathered} ( \frac{r}{100} )^{2} ( 100 )^{2} + \frac{2 r}{100} ( 100 )^{2} - 0.0323 ( 100 )^{2} & = 0 \\ \frac{10000 r^{2}}{10000} + \frac{200000 r}{100} - 323 & = 0 \end{gathered}$

$r^{2}+200r-323=0$ **[1]**

> *   *

ii) *The question asks for the answers to be given to 2 decimal places. This is a hint that you should use the quadratic formula.*

> *The quadratic formula: If  *$ax^{2}+bx+c=0$*  then  *$x=\frac{-b\pm\sqrt{b^{2}-4ac}}{2a}$*.*

> *Substitute the values *$a=1,b=200,c=-323\mathrm{and}x=r$* into the quadratic formula.      *

$r = \frac{- ( 200 ) \pm \sqrt{( 200 )^{2} - ( 4 \times 1 \times - 323 )} }{2 \times 1}$

** [1]**

> *Simplify.*

$\begin{gathered} r & = \frac{- 200 \pm \sqrt{40000 - ( - 1292 )} }{2} \\ = \frac{- 200 \pm \sqrt{41292} }{2} \end{gathered}$

> *Consider both solutions.*

$r=\frac{-200+\sqrt{41292}}{2}\mathrm{or}r=\frac{-200-\sqrt{41292}}{2}$

> $r$* **must be positive, so only work out the solution that will lead to a positive value of *$r$*.*

$r=\frac{-200+\sqrt{41292}}{2}=1.6021653....$

**[1]**

parts.problemMd:
Paddy and Anna each invest \$2000 for 5 years. 
Paddy earns simple interest at a rate of 1.25% per year. 
Anna earns compound interest at a rate of $r$% per year. 
At the end of 5 years, Paddy’s investment is worth the same as Anna’s investment.

Calculate the value of $r$.

$r=$................................................
parts.solutionMd:
> *Simple interest is where each year the interest is calculated by finding the percentage of the initial amount invested.*

> *Find 1.25% of \$2000 by dividing 1.25 by 100 to convert to a decimal and then multiplying by the amount.*

$\frac{1.25}{100}\times2000=25$

*For simple interest, \$25 will be the interest for each year.* *Find Paddy's amount after 5 years by adding 5 lots of \$25 to the initial amount.*

$5\times25+2000=2125$

**[1]**

*Compound interest is where each year the interest is calculated by finding the percentage of the current amount.*

*Recall the formula for compound interest *$A = P ( 1 + \frac{r}{100} )^{n}$*.*

*A** is the total final amount.* 
*P **is the initial amount.*
*r** is the interest rate.* 
*n** is the number of years.*

> *Anna's final amount is the same as Paddy's so is also \$2125. Substitute **A** = 2125, **P **= 2000, **n** = 5 to form an equation.*

$2125 = 2000 ( 1 + \frac{r}{100} )^{5}$

** Correct right hand side expression**** [1] **
**Correct equation**** [1]**

> *Divide both sides by 2000.*

$( 1 + \frac{r}{100} )^{5} = \frac{2125}{2000} = 1.0625$

> *Take the 5th root of both sides.*

`1 + r / 100 = fifth sqrt of 1.0625 ) = 1.012198...`

**[1]**

> *Solve the equation by subtracting 1 from both sides and then multiplying both sides by 100. Use the answer button to avoid losing accuracy.*

$\begin{gathered} \frac{r}{100} & = 0.012198... \\ r = 1.2198... \end{gathered}$

> *Round to 3 significant figures.*

$r=1.22$* ***[1]**

The diagram shows a shape *ABCDEF* made from two rectangles. The total area of the shape is 342 cm<sup>2</sup>.

parts.solutionMd:
> *Split the shape into two rectangles by extending the line **ED**..*

> *Find the length **EF** by subtracting the length of **CD **from the length **AB.*

$2 x - ( x + 3 ) = 2 x - x - 3 = x - 3$

![cie-igcse-2020-may-jun-p4-tz3-q5a-ma](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/SyllabAI/syllabai-resources/3b2ce8da700b80f51700fb34fc721c90d6654d6b/SME-ExamQuestion/cie-igcse-maths-international-maths-23-extended/algebra-and-sequences/forming-and-solving-equations/assets/011-cie-igcse-2020-may-jun-p4-tz3-q5a-ma.png)

**[1]**

> *Find the area of the top rectangle by multiplying the lengths **AF** and **EF**.*

$( x + 1 ) ( x - 3 ) = x^{2} - 3 x + x - 3 = x^{2} - 2 x - 3$

**[1]**

> *Find the area of the bottom rectangle by multiplying the lengths **BC** and **CD**.*

$( 4 x - 5 ) ( x + 3 ) = 4 x^{2} + 12 x - 5 x - 15 = 4 x^{2} + 7 x - 15$

**[1]**

> *Form an equation by adding the two areas together and making the expression equal to 342.*

$( x^{2} - 2 x - 3 ) + ( 4 x^{2} + 7 x - 15 ) = 342$

**[1]**

> *Simplify the expression by collecting like terms.*

$5x^{2}+5x-18=342$

> *Subtract 342 from both sides.*

$5x^{2}+5x-360=0$

> *Factorise out a 5 from the quadratic.*

$5 ( x^{2} + x - 72 ) = 0$

> *Divide both sides by 5.*

$x^{2}+x-72=0$ **[1]**

> *The coefficient of **x*<sup>*2*</sup>* is 1, this means the quadratic will factorise into the form *$( x + p ) ( x + q )$* where **p** and **q **are two numbers which add together to give the coefficient of **x **(1) and multiply together to give the constant term (-72).*

> *The product of the two numbers is negative and the sum is positive, therefore the two numbers have different signs. Look for pairs of numbers that multiply to give -72 and add to make 1.*

$\begin{gathered} 9 \times ( - 8 ) & = 72 \\ 9 + ( - 8 ) & = 1 \end{gathered}$

**[1]**

> *Therefore **p **and **q **are 9 and -8 so you can write in factorised form.*

$( x + 9 ) ( x - 8 ) = 0$

**[1]**

> *Find the two solutions by making each factor equal to zero and solving for **x**.*

$\begin{gathered} x + 9 & = 0 \Leftrightarrow x = - 9 \\ x - 8 & = 0 \Leftrightarrow x = 8 \end{gathered}$

$x=-9\mathrm{or}x=8$ **[1]**

$18<8n$

$\frac{9}{4}$* = 2.25 and the next integer greater than 2.25 is 3. *

parts.problemMd:
The following table of data represents the length, $x$ and area, $y$ of some irregular shapes.

| $x$ | 1 | 5 | $b$ |
|---|---|---|---|
| $y$ | $a$ | 5 | 20 |

Given that $y$ is proportional to the square of $x$, find the values of $a$and $b$.
parts.solutionMd:
> *As *$y$* is proportional to the square of *$x$* we can write the equation*

$y\propto x^{2}\,y=kx^{2}$

> *Substitute the pair of known values into the equation *

$5=k\times5^{2}$

> *Solve the equation to find *$k$

$5=25k\,k=\frac{5}{25}=\frac{1}{5}$

> *So the full equation of the variation model is*

$y=\frac{1}{5}x^{2}$

> *Substitute *$x=1$* in to find *$a$

$\begin{gathered} y = 1 \frac{1}{5} ( 1 )^{2} \\ = 1 \frac{1}{5} \end{gathered}$

$a=\frac{1}{5}$**[1]**

> *Substitute *$y=20$* in to find *$b$

$\begin{gathered} 20 = 1 \frac{1}{5} ( b )^{2} \\ 100 = b^{2} \\ b = \sqrt{100} = \pm 10 \end{gathered}$

> *We know that *$b$* represents the area of a shape, so it must be positive*

** **$b=10$** ****[1]**

> *"*$y\propto\frac{1}{\sqrt{x}}$*" means "*$y$* is directly proportional to one over root *$x$*" or  *$y=k\times\frac{1}{\sqrt{x}}$

> *Substitute *$y=8$* and *$x=4$* into this model*

$8=k\times\frac{1}{\sqrt{4}}$

**[1]**

> *Solve for *$k$
*Start by finding the square root of 4, which is 2*

$8=k\times\frac{1}{2}$

> *Multiply both sides by 2 to get rid of the fraction*

$16=k$

> *Write the direct proportion formula again but replacing *$k$* with 16*

$y=16\times\frac{1}{\sqrt{x}}\mathrm{or}y=\frac{16}{\sqrt{x}}$

**[1]**

> *Now we can find *$y$* when *$x=49$* by substituting  *$x=49$*  into the formula above and evaluating*

$x=49,y=\frac{16}{\sqrt{49}}\,=\frac{16}{7}$

$y=\frac{16}{7}\mathrm{or}2\frac{2}{7}$ ** [1]**

parts.solutionMd:
> *This is inverse proportion, write a formula in terms of *$x,y$* and *$k$

$y\propto\frac{1}{\sqrt{x+1}}$

**[1]**

> *Substitute the given values *$x=8$* and *$y=5$

$5=\frac{k}{\sqrt{8+1}}$

> *Rearrange to find the value of  *$k$

$\begin{gathered} 5 = \frac{k}{ \sqrt{9} } \\ 5 = \frac{k}{3} \\ k = 15 \end{gathered}$

> *Substitute this value of  *$k$* back into the formula*

$y=\frac{15}{\sqrt{x+1}}$**[1]**

> *As *$y$* and *$(x-4)$*are directly proportional, a formula for *$y$* can be found by multiplying a constant (of proportionality) by  *$(x-4)$

$y = k ( x - 4 )$

**[1]**

> *Substitute *$x=16$* and*$y=3$* into the formula to form an equation*

$\begin{gathered} 3 = k ( 16 - 4 ) \\ 3 = 12 k \end{gathered}$

> *Solve the equation to find the value of *$k$

$\begin{array}{rcl} 12 k & = 3 \\ k = \frac{3}{12} = 1 \frac{1}{4} \end{array}$

> *Substitute the value of *$k$* back into the formula for *$y$

$y=\frac{1}{4}(x-4)$ **[1] **

> *Inverse proportion links *$y$* to *$x^{3}$* by*

$y=\frac{k}{x^{3}}$

**[1]**

*We need to find the value of *$k$

$\begin{array}{rcl} 0.5 & = \frac{k}{2^{3}} \\ 0.5 & = \frac{k}{8} \end{array}$

> *Solve to find *$k$* (by multiplying both sides by 8)*

$\begin{gathered} 8 \times 0.5 & = k \\ 4 = k \end{gathered}$

> *Substitute *$k=4$* into the original equation*

$y=\frac{4}{x^{3}}$**[1]**

**The answer is not **$k=4$** as the question asks for ****y**** in terms of ****x**

> *Rewrite the direct proportion statement in terms of *$x,y$* and *$k$*, the constant of proportionality*

$y=k(x-1)^{2}$

**[1]**

> *Now substitute in the first given values *$x=3$* and *$y=24$*, and solve to find *$k$

$\begin{gathered} 24 = k ( 3 - 1 )^{2} \\ 24 = k \times 2^{2} \\ 24 = 4 k \\ k = \frac{24}{4} = 6 \end{gathered}$

> *Now we can replace *$k$* with *$6$* in the general formula*

$y=6(x-1)^{2}$

**[1]**

> *Now substitute your second given value, *$x=6$*, back into the general formula, to find *$y$

$\begin{gathered} y = 6 ( 6 - 1 )^{2} \\ = 6 \times 5^{2} \\ = 6 \times 25 \end{gathered}$

$\begin{gathered} y = 150 \end{gathered}$** [1]**

**[1]**

*Expand the brackets (by multiplying the terms inside by **t**)* * *

$ty+2t=2-3y$ * *

*Collect the **y** terms on one side (for example, by adding 3**y** to both sides then subtracting 2**t **from both sides)* * *

$\begin{gathered} t y + 2 t + 3 y & = 2 \\ t y + 3 y & = 2 - 2 t \end{gathered}$

**[1]**

*Factorise** y** out of the terms on the left* * *

parts.problemMd:
Make *m* the subject of

$\frac{m}{v}-\frac{t}{b}=\frac{m-t}{R}$
parts.solutionMd:
*Get rid of fractions (by multiplying both sides by **bvR**)* * *

$\begin{gathered} b v R ( \frac{m}{v} - \frac{t}{b} ) & = b v R \times \frac{( m - t )}{R} \\ \\ \frac{b \cancel{v} R m}{ \cancel{v} } - \frac{ \cancel{b} v R t}{ \cancel{b} } & = \frac{b v \cancel{R} ( m - t )}{ \cancel{R} } \\ \\ b R m - v R t & = b v ( m - t ) \end{gathered}$

**[1]**

*Expand the brackets on the right* * *

$bRm-vRt=bvm-bvt$ * *

*Move all the **m** terms on to one side (for example, by subtracting **bvm** from both sides then adding **vRt** to both sides)* * *

$\begin{array}{rcl} b R m - v R t - b v m & = - b v t \\ b R m - b v m & = v R t - b v t \end{array}$

**[1]**

*Factorise **m** out of the terms on the left* * *

$m ( b R - b v ) = v R t - b v t$

**[1]**

> *Get **m** on its own (by dividing both sides by **bR - bv**)*

$m=\frac{vRt-bvt}{bR-bv}$* ***[1]**

$m=\frac{bvt-vRt}{bv-bR}$* ***is also accepted**

**n***th term =* $-4n+b$

$\begin{array}{rcl} 11 = - 4 ( 1 ) + b \\ 11 = - 4 + b \\ 15 = b \end{array}$

$\begin{gathered} n \text{th} \text{term} & = 11 + ( n - 1 ) \times ( - 4 ) \\ = 11 + ( - 4 ) ( n - 1 ) \\ = 11 - 4 ( n - 1 ) \end{gathered}$

parts.problemMd:

parts.solutionMd:
> *This question says 'you must show all your working', so show a clear algebraic method and then check on your calculator*

> *Number the equations*

$\begin{gathered} x^{2} + y^{2} & = 9 ( 1 ) \\ x + y & = 2 ( 2 ) \end{gathered}$

> *There is one quadratic equation and one linear equation so this must be done by substitution*

> *Rearrange equation (2) so that the subject is either *$x$* or *$y$* *

> *In this case the subject is *$y$

$\begin{gathered} y & = 2 - x ( 2 ) \end{gathered}$

> *Substitute this into equation (1) to eliminate *$y$

$x^{2} + ( 2 - x )^{2} = 9$

**[1]**

> *Expand the brackets, remember that a bracket squared should be treated the same as double brackets*

$x^{2} + ( 2 - x ) ( 2 - x ) = 9
x^{2 } + 4 - 2 x - 2 x + x^{2 } = 9$

> *Simplify*

$\begin{gathered} x^{2 } + 4 - 4 x + x^{2 } & = 9 \\ 2 x^{2 } - 4 x + 4 & = 9 \end{gathered}$

**Correct expansion**** [1]**

> *Rearrange to form a quadratic equation that is equal to zero*

$\begin{gathered} 2 x^{2 } - 4 x + 4 - 9 & = 0 \\ 2 x^{2 } - 4 x - 5 & = 0 \end{gathered}$

**[1]**

> *The question asks for answers to be given correct to 2 decimal places *

> *This is a hint that the quadratic cannot be factorised and the quadratic formula should be used*

*Find the values of *$a$*, *$b$* and *$c$

$a=2,b=-4,c=-5$

> *Substitute into the quadratic formula*

$x = \frac{- ( - 4 ) \pm \sqrt{( - 4 )^{2} - 4 \times 2 \times ( - 5 )} }{2 \times 2}$

**[1]**

$x = \frac{4 \pm \sqrt{16 - ( - 40 )} }{4} = \frac{4 \pm \sqrt{56} }{4}$

$x=2.870828...,x=-0.870828...$

**[1]**

> *Substitute the values of *$x$* **into one of the equations (the linear equation is easier) to find the values of *$y$

> *Use more than 2 decimal places so that your answers for *$y$* are accurate*

*  *$\begin{gathered} ( 2 ) y_{1} & = 2 - x_{1} = 2 - 2.870828... \\ y_{2} & = 2 - x_{2} = 2 - ( - 0.870828... ) \end{gathered}$

*Round your answers to **two decimal places***       **

Solve the equations

$x=2y+6$

parts.solutionMd:
> *This question says 'you must show all your working', so show a clear algebraic method and then check on your calculator*

> *Number the equations*

$x^{2} + y^{2} = 36 ( 1 )
x = 2 y + 6 ( 2 )$

> *There is one quadratic equation and one linear equation so this must be done by substitution*

> *Equation (2) is equal to *$x$* so this can be eliminated by substituting it into the *$x$* part for equation (1)*
*Substitute *$x=2y+6$* into equation (1)*

$( 2 y + 6 )^{2} + y^{2} = 36$

**[1]**

> *Expand the brackets, remember that a bracket squared should be treated the same as double brackets*

$( 2 y + 6 ) ( 2 y + 6 ) + y^{2} = 36
4 y^{2 } + 6 ( 2 y ) + 6 ( 2 y ) + 6^{2} + y^{2 } = 36$

**[1]**

> *Simplify*

$\begin{gathered} 4 y^{2 } + 12 y + 12 y + 36 + y^{2 } & = 36 \\ 5 y^{2 } + 24 y + 36 & = 36 \end{gathered}$

**[1]**

> *Rearrange to form a quadratic equation that is equal to zero*

$\begin{gathered} 5 y^{2 } + 24 y + 36 - 36 & = 0 \\ 5 y^{2} + 24 y & = 0 \end{gathered}$

> *The question does not give a specified degree of accuracy, so this can be factorised*
*Take out the common factor of *$\begin{array}{rcl} y \end{array}$

$\begin{gathered} y ( 5 y + 24 ) & = 0 \end{gathered}$

> *Solve to find the values of *$y$
*Let each factor be equal to 0 and solve*

$\begin{gathered} y_{1} & = 0 \\ 5 y_{2} + 24 & = 0 \Leftrightarrow y_{2} = - \frac{24}{5} = - 4.8 \end{gathered}$

**[1]**

> *Substitute the values of *$y$* **into one of the equations (the linear equation is easier) to find the values of *$x$

$x_{1} = 2 ( 0 ) + 6 = 6 x_{2} = 2 ( - \frac{24}{5} ) + 6 = - 9.6 + 6$

$x_{1}=6,y_{1}=0$**       **$x_{2}=-3.6,y_{2}=-4.8$** [1]**

Solve the simultaneous equations.
