$\begin{gathered} p + 0.17 + 0.18 + 0.09 + 0.15 + 0.1 & = 1 \\ p & = 1 - ( 0.17 + 0.18 + 0.09 + 0.15 + 0.1 ) \\ p & = 0.31 \end{gathered}$*                          *

**[1]**

> *The probability of landing on 1 OR 3 is the sum of the probability of landing on 1 and the probability of landing on 3. *
*To work out an estimate for the number of times the dice will land on 1 or 3, multiply that total probability by the number of times Neymar rolls the biased dice:  *

$200 \times ( 0.31 + 0.18 )$

**[1]**

$\frac{5}{14}\times140$

> *Use this to form an equation for the probability of taking a green disc.*

**[1]**

**26 pink discs**** ****[1]**

**[1]**

parts.problemMd:
There are some counters in a bag. The counters are red or white or blue or yellow.

Bob is going to take at random a counter from the bag.

The table shows each of the probabilities that the counter will be blue or will be yellow.

| **Colour** | red | white | blue | yellow |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Probability** |   |   | 0.45 | 0.25 |

There are 18 blue counters in the bag.

The probability that the counter Bob takes will be red is twice the probability that the counter will be white.

Work out the number of red counters in the bag.
parts.solutionMd:
> *We can use the fact that the total of all the probabilities must sum to 1. *
*The probability of taking a red counter is twice the probability of taking a white counter. *
*So if the probability of taking a white counter is '**p'**, then the probability of taking a red counter will be '2**p'**. Set up an equation with all the probabilities:*

$\begin{gathered} 2 p + p + 0.45 + 0.25 & = 1 \\ 2 p + p & = 1 - ( 0.45 + 0.25 ) \end{gathered}$*                          *

**[1]**

> *Solve the equation to find the values of **p** and 2**p:*

> $\begin{gathered} 3 p & = 0.3 \\ p & = 0.3 \div 3 \\ p & = 0.1 \end{gathered}$* *

$\begin{gathered} \mathrm{P} ( \text{red} ) & = 2 p = 2 \times 0.1 = 0.2 \end{gathered}$

**[1]**

> *The ratio of the probability of taking a red counter to the probability of taking a blue counter is the same as the ratio of the number of red counters to the number of blue counters. There are 18 blue counters, and the probability of taking a blue counter is 0.45. *
*We don't know the number of red counters, so call that **n**. We know that the probability of taking a red counter is 0.2. *
*Write down the ratio, turn it into an equation with fractions, and solve for **n**.*

$\begin{gathered} n : 18 & = 0.2 : 0.45 \\ \frac{n}{18} & = \frac{0.2}{0.45} \\ n & = 18 \times \frac{0.2}{0.45} \\ n & = 8 \end{gathered}$

**[1]**

**8 red counters****  ****[1]**

$\mathrm{Paul} \mathrm{heads}:\mathrm{tails}=80:40=2:1=\mathrm{twice} \mathrm{as} \mathrm{likely}\,\,\mathrm{Ben} \mathrm{heads}:\mathrm{tails}=34:8=17:4=\mathrm{more} \mathrm{than}4\mathrm{times} \mathrm{as} \mathrm{likely}\,\,\mathrm{Helen} \mathrm{heads}:\mathrm{tails}=66:12=33:6=\mathrm{more} \mathrm{than}5\mathrm{times} \mathrm{as} \mathrm{likely}\,\,\mathrm{Sharif} \mathrm{heads}:\mathrm{tails}=120:40=3:1=3\mathrm{times} \mathrm{as} \mathrm{likely}\,$*                          *

The coin is to be thrown twice.

Use all the results in the table to work out an estimate for the probability that the coin will land heads both times.
parts.solutionMd:
> *First find the relative frequency (i.e., experimental probability) for 'heads', by dividing the total number of times the coin landed on heads by the total number of times it was thrown. Then multiply that relative frequency by itself to determine an estimate for the probability the coin will land on heads the first time and then on heads again the second time.*

$\mathrm{P} ( \text{heads} ) = \frac{34 + 66 + 80 + 120}{34 + 66 + 80 + 120 + 8 + 12 + 40 + 40} = \frac{300}{400} = \frac{3}{4} 

 \frac{3}{4} \times \frac{3}{4} = \frac{9}{16}$*                          *

**[1]**

$\frac{9}{16}$**  ****[1]**

parts.problemMd:
Becky has a biased 6-sided dice.

The table gives information about the probability that, when the dice is thrown, it will land on each number.

| **  Number** | 1 | 2 | 3 | 4 | 5 | 6 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **  Probability** | $2x$ | 0.18 | $2x$ | $3x$ | 0.26 | $x$ |

Becky is going to throw the dice 200 times.

Work out an estimate for the number of times that the dice will land on an even number.
parts.solutionMd:
> *Use the fact that all probabilities must sum to 1 to set up an equation in **x**.*

$\begin{gathered} 2 x + 0.18 + 2 x + 3 x + 0.26 + x & = 1 \end{gathered}$

**[1]**

> *Now collect terms and solve the equation to find the value of **x**.*

$\begin{gathered} 8 x + 0.44 & = 1 \\ 8 x & = 1 - 0.44 \\ 8 x & = 0.56 \\ x & = 0.56 \div 8 \\ x & = 0.07 \end{gathered}$

**[1]**

> *The probability of getting an even number is equal to the sum of the probabilities for 2, 4 and 6.*

$\begin{gathered} \mathrm{P} ( \text{even} ) & = 0.18 + 3 x + x \\ = 0.18 + 4 x \\ = 0.18 + 4 ( 0.07 ) \\ = 0.46 \end{gathered}$

> *Now we can estimate the number of times Becky gets an even number by multiplying the number of times she is going to throw the dice by the probability that the dice will land on an even number.*

*200 × 0.46*

**[1]**

**92****  [1]**

*So the numerator is 4*

**Identifying denominator as 50, or numerator as 4****  [1]**

$\frac{4}{50}\mathrm{or}\frac{2}{25}$**[1]**

parts.problemMd: A box contains 7 black pens and 8 orange pens. Two pens are chosen at random from this box without replacement. Calculate the probability that at least one orange pen is chosen.

*Method 1* *This is the most efficient method, if you spot that the only way at least pen **isn't** orange is if both pens are black. So*

$\begin{gathered} P ( \text{at} \text{least} \text{one} \text{orange} ) & = 1 - \mathrm{P} ( \text{both} \text{black} ) \\ = 1 - ( \frac{7}{15} \times \frac{6}{14} ) \end{gathered}$

**[2]**

$=\frac{168}{210}\mathrm{or}\frac{4}{5}$** [1]**

**Giving your answer as another equivalent fraction, or as 0.8 or 80%, is acceptable**

*Method 2* *Identify all the ways that at least one orange pens can be picked*

$\begin{gathered} P ( \text{orange} \text{then} \text{black} ) = ( \frac{7}{15} \times \frac{8}{14} ) , P ( \text{black} \text{then} \text{orange} ) = ( \frac{8}{15} \times \frac{7}{14} ) , P ( \text{both} \text{orange} ) & = ( \frac{8}{15} \times \frac{7}{14} ) \end{gathered}$

**one of these multiplications is seen ****[1]**

> *Add together all the ways that at least one orange pen can be picked*

$\begin{gathered} ( \frac{7}{15} \times \frac{8}{14} ) + ( \frac{8}{15} \times \frac{7}{14} ) + ( \frac{8}{15} \times \frac{7}{14} ) \end{gathered}$

$\frac{168}{210}\mathrm{or}\frac{4}{5}$** ****[1]**

parts.problemMd:
A box contains 15 red pencils, 8 yellow pencils and 2 green pencils. 
Two pencils are picked at random without replacement.
 Find the probability that at least one pencil is red.
parts.solutionMd:
> *The first pencil is not replaced before the second pencil is chosen, so the events are conditional and the probabilities will change. *

> *This is best represented using a probability tree diagram.*

> *As the problem only concerns red or not red pencils, it is easiest to group the yellow and green together and call them not red pencils.*

*Total number of pencils = 15 + 8 + 2 = 25** *
*Total number of red pencils = 15** *
*Total number of not red pencils = 25 - 15 = 10  *

![cie-igcse-2020-oct-nov-p4-tz1-q9d-working](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/SyllabAI/syllabai-resources/3b2ce8da700b80f51700fb34fc721c90d6654d6b/SME-ExamQuestion/cie-igcse-maths-international-maths-23-extended/probability/tree-diagrams-and-multiple-events/assets/016-cie-igcse-2020-oct-nov-p4-tz1-q9d-working.png)

> *Method 1*

> *Subtract the probability that both pencils are not red from 1.*

$\begin{gathered} 1 - \mathrm{P} ( \text{Both} \text{not} \text{red} ) \\ = 1 - ( \frac{10}{25} \times \frac{9}{ 24} ) \end{gathered}$

**[2]**

$\frac{17}{20}$** [1] **
**Unsimplified fraction or equivalent correct decimal accepted.**

> *Method 2*

> *Add the probability of both being red to the probability of one being red and the other being not red. *
*P(at least one red) = P(both red) + P(first red, second not red) + P(first not red, second red).*

$( \frac{15}{25} \times \frac{14}{ 24} ) + ( \frac{15}{25} \times \frac{10}{ 24} ) + ( \frac{10}{25} \times \frac{15}{ 24} )$

** ****At least one correct product**** [1]  **
**All three correct and added together**** [1]**

$\frac{17}{20}$** [1] **
**Unsimplified fraction or equivalent correct decimal accepted.**

i) Jojo chooses two cards at random from Set *A* without replacement. 
Find the probability that the two cards have the same number.

[3]

ii) Jojo replaces the two cards. Kylie then chooses one card at random from Set *A* and one card at random from Set *B*. 
Find the probability that the two cards have the same number.

[3]

iii) Who is the most likely to choose two cards that have the same number? Show all your working.

[1]
parts.solutionMd:
> *The probability of an event X happening is given by: P(X) = *$\frac{\mathrm{number} \mathrm{of} \mathrm{ways} \mathrm{event} \mathrm{can} \mathrm{happen}}{\mathrm{total} \mathrm{number} \mathrm{of} \mathrm{possible} \mathrm{events}}$*.*

> *The probability of event X and event Y happening is given by: P(X and Y) = P(X) × P(Y).*

> *The probability of event X or event Y happening is given by: P(X or Y) = P(X) + P(Y).*

i) *The two cards can be the same number if; *

> *Option1: Jojo picks a 1 and then another 1. *
*The probability of a 1 first time is *$\frac{2}{5}$*, but the second time there is one less 1 and one less card to choose from so the probability is *

$\frac{2-1}{5-1}=\frac{1}{4}$

> *So the probability of choosing a 1 then a 1 is *

*P(1 and 1)*$= \frac{2}{5} \times 1 \frac{1}{4} ( = \frac{2}{20} )$

> *Option2: Jojo picks a 2 and then another 2. *
*The probability of a 2 first time is *$\frac{3}{5}$*, but the second time there is one less 2 and one less card to choose from so the probability is *

$\frac{3-1}{5-1}=\frac{2}{4}$

> *So the probability of choosing a 2 then a 2 is *

*P(2 and 2)*$= \frac{3}{5} \times \frac{2}{4} ( = \frac{6}{20} )$

**either**** **$"\frac{2}{5}\times\frac{1}{4}"$** or **$"\frac{3}{5}\times\frac{2}{4}"$** ****[1]**

> *Therefore the probability of (1 and 1) **or** (2 and 2) is*

** **$\frac{2}{5} \times 1 \frac{1}{4} + \frac{3}{5} \times \frac{2}{4} ( = \frac{2}{20} + \frac{6}{20} )$

**[1]**

$=\frac{8}{20}$

**Answer = **$\frac{2}{5}$** or 0.4 or 40% ****[1] **
**Any equivalent fraction, such as **$\frac{8}{20}$**, is accepted**

ii) *The two cards can be the same number if; *

> *Option1: Set A is a 1 and  Set B is a 1. We'll refer to this as A1 and B1.*

> *Option 2: Set A is a 2 and Set B is a 2. We'll refer to this as A2 and B2. For Option 1 above, P(A1) =*$\frac{2}{5}$* and P(B1) =*$\frac{3}{5}$*. *
*For Option 2 above, P(A2) =*$\frac{3}{5}$* and P(B2) =*$\frac{1}{5}$*.*

> *Therefore:*

*P(A1 and B1)*$= \frac{2}{5} \times \frac{3}{5} ( = \frac{6}{25} )$*     and    P(A2 and B2)*$= \frac{3}{5} \times 1 \frac{1}{5} ( = \frac{3}{25} )$* *

* ***either of these calculations ****[1]**

> *Therefore the probability of A1 and B2, or A2 and B2 happening is:*

*P[(A1 and B1) or (A2 and B2)]*$= \frac{2}{5} \times \frac{3}{5} + \frac{3}{5} \times 1 \frac{1}{5} ( = \frac{6}{25} + \frac{3}{25} )$** **

**[1]**

**Answer =**$\frac{9}{25}$** ****or 0.36 or 36% ****[1]**

iii) *From part (a)(i) we know that the probability of Jojo picking two cards that have the same number is *$\frac{2}{5}$* and the probability of Kylie picking two cards that the have the same number is *$\frac{9}{25}$*. We need to decide which of these two fractions is bigger.*

> *Method 1*

> *Write both fractions with the same numerator.*
* The lowest common numerator is 25.*

*Jojo: *$\frac{2}{5}=\frac{10}{25}$*      Kylie: *$\frac{9}{25}$

$\frac{10}{25}>\frac{9}{25}$

> *Therefore Jojo is more likely to pick two cards that have the same number.*

$\frac{10}{25}>\frac{9}{25}$** therefore Jojo** **[1]**

**You must show a reason, e.g. **$"\frac{10}{25}>\frac{9}{25}"$** to achieve the mark**

> *Method 2*

> *Convert both fractions to decimals. *
*You can do this directly on your calculator if necessary.*

*Jojo: *$\frac{2}{5}=0.4$*      Kylie: *$\frac{9}{25}=0.36$

$0.4>0.36$

> *Therefore Jojo is more likely to pick two cards that have the same number.*

$0.4>0.36$** therefore Jojo**** ****[1]**

**You must show a reason, e.g. "0.4 > 0.36" to achieve the mark**

> *The formula for the cosine rule is *$a^{2}=b^{2}+c^{2}-2bc\mathrm{cos}A$*, where **b** and **c** are the lengths of the two sides that form angle **A** and **a** is the length of the side opposite **A**. Substitute **a** = **AB**, **b** = 6, **c** = 7 and **A** = 60 into the formula.*

$\begin{gathered} A B^{2} & = 6^{2} + 7^{2} - 2 ( 6 ) ( 7 ) \cos ( 60 ) \\ = 36 + 49 - 84 \cos ( 60 ) \\ = 85 - 84 \cos ( 60 ) \end{gathered}$

**[1]**

$\cos ( 60 ) = 1 \frac{1}{2}$

$\begin{gathered} A B^{2} & = 85 - 84 \times 1 \frac{1}{2} \\ = 85 - 42 \\ = 43 \end{gathered}$

**[1]**

> *Take the positive square root of both sides. Remember to include units for the length.*

`A B = | _ _ sqrt( 43 | | cm`* ***[1]**

parts.solutionMd:
> *You can find the angle between the sides **AC** and **AB** by spotting that the three interior angles of the triangle should add up to 180°.*

$\begin{gathered} \text{Angle} B A C & = 180 - 64 - 49 \\ = 67 \end{gathered}$

> *To find the area of a triangle you need to know the lengths of two sides and the angle between them.*

> *You know the length of one side and the angle opposite it. You also know another angle so you can find the length of the side opposite that using the sine rule.*

> *The formula for the sine rule is *$\frac{a}{\mathrm{sin}A}=\frac{b}{\mathrm{sin}B}$*, where **a** and **b** are the lengths of the two sides that are opposite the angles **A **and **B **respectively. Substitute **a** = **AC**, **b** = 8.7, **A** = 49 and **B** = 64 into the formula.*

$\frac{A C}{\sin ( 49 )} = \frac{8.7}{\sin ( 64 )}$

**[1]**

> *Multiply both sides by sin(49) and type into your calculator.*

$\begin{gathered} A C & = \frac{8.7}{\sin ( 64 )} \times \sin ( 49 ) \\ = 7.305314... \end{gathered}$

*Rearranging correctly** ***[1] **

*Correct answer** ***[1]**

> *The formula for the area of a triangle is *$\mathrm{Area}=\frac{1}{2}ab\mathrm{sin}C$*, where **a** and **b** are the lengths of the two sides that form angle **C**. Substitute **a** = 7.305314... (using the answer button), **b** = 8.7 and **C** = 67 into the formula.*

$\begin{gathered} \text{Area} = 1 \frac{1}{2} \times 7.305314... \times 8.7 \times \sin ( 67 ) \end{gathered}$

**[1]**

> *Type into your calculator.*

$\begin{array}{rcl} \text{Area} = 29.251912... \end{array}$

> *Round to 3 significant figures. Remember to include the units for the area.*

$\mathrm{Area}=29.3\mathrm{cm}^{2}(3\mathrm{sf})$ **[1]**

parts.solutionMd:
> *Finding the angle opposite the side **LN** will help you.*

> *You know the length of one side and the angle opposite it. You also know the length of another side so you can use the sine rule to find the angle opposite it.*

> *The formula for the sine rule is *$\frac{\mathrm{sin}A}{a}=\frac{\mathrm{sin}B}{b}$*, where **a** and **b** are the lengths of the two sides that are opposite the angles **A **and **B **respectively. *

> *Substitute **a** = **12.8**, **b** = 15.7, **A** = **MLN** and **B** = 136 into the formula.*

$\frac{\sin ( M L N )}{12.8} = \frac{\sin ( 136 )}{15.7}$

**[1]**

> *Multiply both sides by 12.8 and then find the angle by using the inverse sin function.*

$\begin{gathered} \sin ( M L N ) & = \frac{\sin ( 136 )}{15.7} \times 12.8 \\ M L N & = \sin ^{- 1} ( \frac{\sin ( 136 )}{15.7} \times 12.8 ) \end{gathered}$

**[1]**

> *Type into your calculator.*

$\begin{gathered} M L N & = 34.495789... \end{gathered}$

**[1]**

> *You can find the angle between the sides **LM** and **MN** by spotting that the three interior angles of the triangle should add up to 180°. Use the answer button on your calculator.*

$\begin{gathered} \text{Angle} L M N & = 180 - 136 - 34.495789... \\ = 9.504210... \end{gathered}$

> *You now have enough information to find the side **LN** using either the sine rule or the cosine rule.*

> *Method 1 - Using the sine rule*

> *The formula for the sine rule is *$\frac{a}{\mathrm{sin}A}=\frac{b}{\mathrm{sin}B}$*, where **a** and **b** are the lengths of the two sides that are opposite the angles **A **and **B **respectively. *

> *Substitute **a** = **LN**, **b** = 15.7, **A** = 9.504210... (using the answer button) and **B** = 136 into the formula.*

$\frac{L N}{\sin ( 9.504210... )} = \frac{15.7}{\sin ( 136 )}$

**[1]**

> *Multiply both sides by sin(9.504210...) and type into your calculator.*

$\begin{gathered} L N & = \frac{15.7}{\sin ( 136 )} \times \sin ( 9.504210... ) \\ = 3.731885... \end{gathered}$

> *Round to 3 significant figures. Remember to include the units for the length.*

$LN=3.73\mathrm{cm}(3\mathrm{sf})$** [1]**

> *Method 2 - Using the cosine rule*

> *The formula for the cosine rule is *$a^{2}=b^{2}+c^{2}-2bc\mathrm{cos}A$*, where **b** and **c** are the lengths of the two sides that form angle **A** and **a** is the length of the side opposite **A**. *

> *Substitute **a** = **LN**, **b** = 15.7, **c** = 12.8 and **A** = 9.504210... (using the answer button) into the formula.*

$L N^{2} = 15.7^{2} + 12.8^{2} - 2 ( 15.7 ) ( 12.8 ) \cos ( 9.504210... )$

**[1]**

> *Type the expression into your calculator altogether as one line. If you do it separately you need to remember the order of operations (multiplication before addition).*

$LN^{2}=13.926966...$

> *Take the positive square root of both sides.*

$\begin{gathered} L N & = \sqrt{13.926966...} \\ = 3.731885... \end{gathered}$

> *Round to 3 significant figures. Remember to include the units for the length.*

$LN=3.73\mathrm{cm}(3\mathrm{sf})$** [1]**

The diagram shows a trapezium $ABCD$.

$AB$ is parallel to $DC$.

$AB=55m$, $BD=70m$, angle $ABD=40^{\circ}$ and angle $BCD=32^{\circ}$.

Calculate $AD$.

$AD=$ ........................................... m
parts.solutionMd:
> *Use triangle *$ABD$* to find the missing side *$AD$*.*

> $AD$* is opposite the given angle and the two other sides are known so the cosine rule should be used.*

> *Substitute the values of  *$a=55,b=70\mathrm{and}C=40^{\circ}$* into the cosine rule. *

> *Cosine Rule:  *$c^{2}=a^{2}+b^{2}-2ab\mathrm{cos}C$*.*

> $c^{2 } = 55^{2 } + 70^{2 } - 2 ( 55 ) ( 70 ) \cos 40$*  *

**Correct use of equation**** [1] **

**Substitute values into the equation**** ****correctly**** ****[1]**

> *Use your calculator to find the value of *$c^{2}$*.*

$c^{2}=2026.45778...$

**[1]**

> *Square root to find the value of *$c$*.*

$\begin{gathered} c^{ } & = \sqrt{ 2026.45778...} \\ = 45.0161... \end{gathered}$

$c=45.0m(3s.f.)$* ***[1] **

**If not rounded, 45.01 to 45.02 is accepted.**

parts.problemMd:
**Extract:**

The diagram shows a trapezium ABCD. AB is parallel to DC. AB = 55 m, BD = 70 m, angle ABD = 40°, and angle BCD = 32°.

Calculate $BC$.

$BC=$ ........................................... m
parts.solutionMd:
> *Use triangle *$BCD$* to find the missing side *$BC$*.*

> $BC$* is adjacent to the given angle, one other side is known and one more angle is needed to use the sine rule.*

> *The lines *$AB$* and *$DC$* are parallel so angle *$BDC$* is an alternate to angle *$ABD$*. Alternate angles are equal.*

$B \hat{D} C = 40^{\circ}$

**[1]**

> *Substitute the values of  *`B D = 70 , B D -hat C = 40 and B C -hat D = 32 deg`* into the sine rule. *

> *Sine Rule:  *$\frac{a}{\mathrm{sin}A}=\frac{b}{\mathrm{sin}B}=\frac{c}{\mathrm{sin}C}$*.*

$\frac{BC}{\mathrm{sin}40^{\circ}}=\frac{70}{\mathrm{sin}32^{\circ}}$

**[1]**

> *Rearrange the equation to find the value of *$BC.$

$\begin{gathered} B C & = \frac{ 70 \sin 40^{\circ}}{\sin 32^{\circ}} \\ = 84.90941... \end{gathered}$

** ****[1]**

$BC=84.9m(3s.f.)$* ***[1] **

**If not rounded, 84.90 to 84.91 is accepted.**

parts.problemMd:
**Extract:**

The diagram shows a trapezium ABCD. AB is parallel to DC. AB = 55 m, BD = 70 m, angle ABD = 40°, and angle BCD = 32°.

Calculate the area of $ABCD$.

.......................................... m<sup>2</sup>
parts.solutionMd:
> *Find the area of each triangle individually and add them together. Formula for the area of a triangle: *$\mathrm{Area}=\frac{1}{2}ab\mathrm{sin}C$*.*

> *Find the area of triangle *$ABD$*.*

$\begin{gathered} A B D & = 1 \frac{1}{2} ( A B ) ( A D ) \sin ( A \hat{B} D ) \\ = 1 \frac{1}{2} ( 55 ) ( 70 ) \sin ( 40^{\circ} ) \\ = 1925 \sin 40^{\circ} \\ = 1237.366... \end{gathered}$

**[1]**

> *To find the area of triangle *$BCD$* the third angle in the triangle will be needed.*

$\begin{gathered} D \hat{B} C & = 180 - B \hat{C} D - B \hat{D} C \\ = 180 - 32 - 40 \\ = 108^{\circ} \end{gathered}$

> *Area of triangle *$B C D \begin{gathered} = \end{gathered} \begin{gathered} \end{gathered} \begin{gathered} 1 \frac{1}{2} \end{gathered} \begin{gathered} \end{gathered} \begin{gathered} ( B C ) \end{gathered} \begin{gathered} ( A D ) \end{gathered} \begin{gathered} \end{gathered} \begin{gathered} \mathrm{s} \end{gathered} \begin{gathered} \mathrm{i} \end{gathered} \begin{gathered} \mathrm{n} \end{gathered} \begin{gathered} \end{gathered} \begin{gathered} ( B C D ) \end{gathered}$*. *

$\begin{gathered} B C D & = 1 \frac{1}{2} ( 84.90941... ) ( 70 ) \sin ( 108^{\circ} ) \\ = 2826.377... \end{gathered}$

**[1]**

> *Add the areas of the two triangles together.*

$\begin{gathered} \text{Area} A B C D & = 1237.366... + 2826.377... \\ = 4063.743... \end{gathered}$

$\begin{array}{ccc} Area A B C D & = & 4060 cm^{ } 2 \text{stretchy} ( 3 s. f. \text{stretchy} )\end{array}$* ***[1] **

**Answers in the range 4063 to 4064 cm**<sup>**2**</sup>** will gain full marks.**

![cie-igcse-2019-may-jun-p4-tz2-q8a](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/SyllabAI/syllabai-resources/3b2ce8da700b80f51700fb34fc721c90d6654d6b/SME-ExamQuestion/cie-igcse-maths-international-maths-23-extended/pythagoras-and-trigonometry/sine-cosine-rule-and-area-of-triangles/assets/069-cie-igcse-2019-may-jun-p4-tz2-q8a.png)

The diagram shows two triangles $ABD$ and $BCD$.

$AD=16.5\text{cm}$ and $BD=12.4\text{cm}$.

Angle $ADB=64^{\circ}$, angle $BDC=53^{\circ}$ and angle $DBC=95^{\circ}$.

i) Find $AB$.

$AB$ = ........................................ cm [4]

ii) Find $BC$.

$BC$ = ........................................ cm [4]
parts.solutionMd:
i) *To find length *$AB$* we can consider triangle *$ABD$* and use the cosine rule:* $a^{2}=b^{2}+c^{2}-2bc\mathrm{cos}A$

> *In this formula, the lower-case sides, *$a,b,c$* must be opposite their respective angles, which are capital letters (in this case only *$A$*)*

*We will re-label the triangle (in red) to reflect this*

![cie-igcse-2019-may-jun-p4-tz2-q8-1](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/SyllabAI/syllabai-resources/3b2ce8da700b80f51700fb34fc721c90d6654d6b/SME-ExamQuestion/cie-igcse-maths-international-maths-23-extended/pythagoras-and-trigonometry/sine-cosine-rule-and-area-of-triangles/assets/070-cie-igcse-2019-may-jun-p4-tz2-q8-1.png)

> *Using the cosine rule*

$a^{2} = 12.4^{2} + 16.5^{2} - ( 2 \times 12.4 \times 16.5 \times \cos ( 64 ) )$

**[2]**

> *Evaluating the right hand side using calculator*

$a^{2}=246.6285267...$

**[1]**

> *Square-rooting (make sure you use the unrounded value)*

$a=\sqrt{246.6285267...}=15.70441106...$

$AB=15.7\mathrm{cm}$ **[1]**

**Rounded to 3 significant figures**

ii) *Considering triangle *$BDC$* (using the original labels), we can find angle *$C$* using the fact that the sum of the interior angles in a triangle is 180°*

$180-95-53=32$

**[1]**

> *We can now use the sine rule, *$\frac{a}{\mathrm{sin}A}=\frac{b}{\mathrm{sin}B}=\frac{c}{\mathrm{sin}C}$* where the sides *$a,b,c$* must be opposite their respective angles, which are capital letters*

![cie-igcse-2019-may-jun-p4-tz2-q8a-2](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/SyllabAI/syllabai-resources/3b2ce8da700b80f51700fb34fc721c90d6654d6b/SME-ExamQuestion/cie-igcse-maths-international-maths-23-extended/pythagoras-and-trigonometry/sine-cosine-rule-and-area-of-triangles/assets/071-cie-igcse-2019-may-jun-p4-tz2-q8a-2.png)

> *Applying the sine rule to *$BDC$* (we are trying to find *$BC$*, labelled as *$d$*)*

$\frac{d}{\sin ( 53 )} = \frac{12.4}{\sin ( 32 )}$

> *Multiply both sides by *$\sin ( 53 )$

$d = \frac{12.4}{\sin ( 32 )} \times \sin ( 53 )$

**[2]**

$d=18.68790398...$

$BC=18.7\mathrm{cm}$ **[1]**

**Rounded to 3 significant figures**

i) Show that $AC$ = 76.7 m, correct to 1 decimal place.

[5]

ii) Calculate $BD$.

$BD$ = .......................................... m

[3]
parts.solutionMd:
a) *Labelling the diagram with the angles of elevation*

![cie-igcse-2019-may-jun-p4-tz2-q9a-1](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/SyllabAI/syllabai-resources/3b2ce8da700b80f51700fb34fc721c90d6654d6b/SME-ExamQuestion/cie-igcse-maths-international-maths-23-extended/pythagoras-and-trigonometry/sine-cosine-rule-and-area-of-triangles/assets/087-cie-igcse-2019-may-jun-p4-tz2-q9a-1.png)

> *The sum of the angles on a straight line is 180°, and we can use this fact to find angle *$ADC$

$ADC=180-72=108$

**[1]**

> *The interior angles in a triangle sum to 180°, and this can be applied to triangle *$ACD$* to find angle *$ACD$

$ACD=180-26-108=46$

**[1]**

![cie-igcse-2019-may-jun-p4-tz2-q9a-2](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/SyllabAI/syllabai-resources/3b2ce8da700b80f51700fb34fc721c90d6654d6b/SME-ExamQuestion/cie-igcse-maths-international-maths-23-extended/pythagoras-and-trigonometry/sine-cosine-rule-and-area-of-triangles/assets/088-cie-igcse-2019-may-jun-p4-tz2-q9a-2.png)

> *To find the length of *$AC$* we can use the sine rule; *$\frac{a}{\mathrm{sin}A}=\frac{b}{\mathrm{sin}B}=\frac{c}{\mathrm{sin}C}$* where the lower-case letters are the side lengths and the upper case letters are the angles opposite those sides*

> *Applying the sine rule to the triangle *$ACD$

$\frac{A C}{\sin ( 108 )} = \frac{58}{\sin ( 46 )}$

> *Multiplying both sides by *$\sin ( 108 )$

$A C = \frac{58}{\sin ( 46 )} \times \sin ( 108 )$

**[2]**

$AC=76.68320023...$

$AC=76.7m$* ***[1]*** *

**Rounded to 1 decimal place**

ii) *Considering the right-angled triangle *$ABC$

![cie-igcse-2019-may-jun-p4-tz2-q9a-3](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/SyllabAI/syllabai-resources/3b2ce8da700b80f51700fb34fc721c90d6654d6b/SME-ExamQuestion/cie-igcse-maths-international-maths-23-extended/pythagoras-and-trigonometry/sine-cosine-rule-and-area-of-triangles/assets/089-cie-igcse-2019-may-jun-p4-tz2-q9a-3.png)

> *As we know the hypotenuse and the angle, we can find the adjacent *$( A B )$* using the cosine ratio; *$\mathrm{cos}θ=\frac{\mathrm{adjacent}}{\mathrm{hypotenuse}}$

$\cos ( 26 ) = \frac{A B}{76.7}$

**[1]**

> *Multiply both sides by 76.7*

$76.7 \times \cos ( 26 ) = A B$

$AB=68.93750335...$

**[1]**

> *We can then find the length *$BD$

$68.93750335-58=10.93750335...$

**10.9 m*** ***[1]*** *

**Round to 3 significant figures**

parts.solutionMd:
> *The formula for the area of a triangle is *$\mathrm{Area}=\frac{1}{2}ab\mathrm{sin}C$*, where **a** and **b** are the lengths of the two sides that form angle **C**. Substitute Area = *$6\sqrt{2}$*, **a** = *$( x + 3 )$*, **b** = *$( 2 x - 1 )$* and **C** = 45 into the formula.*

$\begin{gathered} 6 \sqrt{2} & = 1 \frac{1}{2} \times ( x + 3 ) \times ( 2 x - 1 ) \times \sin ( 45 ) \end{gathered}$

*Correct expression on the right hand side*** [1] **

*Forming a correct equation ***[1]**

> *Use the fact that *$\sin ( 45 ) = \frac{ \sqrt{2} }{2}$*.*

$\begin{gathered} 6 \sqrt{2} & = 1 \frac{1}{2} \times ( x + 3 ) \times ( 2 x - 1 ) \times \frac{ \sqrt{2} }{2} \end{gathered}$

> *Divide both sides by √2 and multiply both sides by 4 to get rid of the surds and denominators.*

$\begin{gathered} 24 = ( x + 3 ) ( 2 x - 1 ) \end{gathered}$

> *Expand the brackets then simplify.*

$2x^{2}-x+6x-3=24\,2x^{2}+5x-3=24$

**[1]**

> *Subtract 24 from both sides to make the quadratic equal 0.*

$2x^{2}+5x-27=0$

> *As the question asks for 3 significant figures, this suggests that the quadratic does not factorise. Solve by using the quadratic formula, *$x=\frac{-b\pm\sqrt{b^{2}-4ac}}{2a}$*. *

> *Substitute **a** = 2, **b** = 5 and **c =** -27 into the formula.*

$\begin{gathered} x = \frac{- 5 \pm \sqrt{5^{2} - 4 ( 2 ) ( - 27 )} }{2 ( 2 )} \end{gathered}$

**[1]**

> *Simplify using your calculator.*

$\begin{gathered} x = \frac{- 5 + \sqrt{241} }{4} = 2.631043... \\ \text{or} \\ x = \frac{- 5 - \sqrt{241} }{4} = - 5.131043... \end{gathered}$

> *As **x** + 3 is a length then it can not be negative, so **x** > -3. Therefore reject **x** = -5.131043... *

> *Round the other solution to 3 significant figures.*

$x=2.63(3sf)$* ***[1]**

parts.solutionMd:
> *First use the area to form an equation using triangle **ADC**.*

![4-11-edexcel-gcse-vhq2-1](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/SyllabAI/syllabai-resources/3b2ce8da700b80f51700fb34fc721c90d6654d6b/SME-ExamQuestion/cie-igcse-maths-international-maths-23-extended/pythagoras-and-trigonometry/sine-cosine-rule-and-area-of-triangles/assets/021-4-11-edexcel-gcse-vhq2-1.png)

> *The formula for the area of a triangle is *$\mathrm{Area}=\frac{1}{2}ab\mathrm{sin}C$*, where **a** and **b** are the lengths of the two sides that form angle **C**. Substitute Area = 56, **a** = **z**, **b** = 11 and **C** = 105 into the formula.*

$\begin{gathered} 56 = 1 \frac{1}{2} \times z \times 11 \times \sin ( 105 ) \end{gathered}$

**[1]**

> *Rearrange to get **z** by itself by multiplying both sides by 2 and dividing both sides by 11sin(105). Type into your calculator.*

$\begin{gathered} z = \frac{56 \times 2}{11 \times \sin ( 105 )} \\ = 10.540993... \end{gathered}$

**[1]**

> *You now know the lengths of two sides and the angle between them and you want to find the length of the third side. Therefore you need to use the cosine rule.*

> *The formula for the cosine rule is *$a^{2}=b^{2}+c^{2}-2bc\mathrm{cos}A$*, where **b** and **c** are the lengths of the two sides that form angle **A** and **a** is the length of the side opposite **A**. *

> *Substitute **a** = **y**, **b** = 11, **c** = 10.540993... (using the answer button) and **A** = 105 into the formula.*

$y^{2} = 11^{2} + 10.540993...^{2} - 2 ( 11 ) ( 10.540993... ) \cos ( 105 )$

**[1]**

> *Type the expression into your calculator altogether as one line. If you do it separately you need to remember the order of operations (multiplication before addition).*

$y^{2}=292.133170...$

> *Take the positive square root of both sides.*

$\begin{array}{rcl} y = \sqrt{292.133170...} \\ = 17.091903... \end{array}$

> *Now use triangle **ABC**. You know the length of a side and the angle opposite it. You also know another angle so you can use the sine rule to find the length of the side opposite it.*

![4-11-edexcel-gcse-vhq2-2](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/SyllabAI/syllabai-resources/3b2ce8da700b80f51700fb34fc721c90d6654d6b/SME-ExamQuestion/cie-igcse-maths-international-maths-23-extended/pythagoras-and-trigonometry/sine-cosine-rule-and-area-of-triangles/assets/022-4-11-edexcel-gcse-vhq2-2.png)

> *The formula for the sine rule is *$\frac{a}{\mathrm{sin}A}=\frac{b}{\mathrm{sin}B}$*, where **a** and **b** are the lengths of the two sides that are opposite the angles **A **and **B **respectively. *

> *Substitute **a** = **x**, **b** = 17.091903... (using the answer button), **A** = 48 and **B** = 118 into the formula.*

$\frac{x}{\sin ( 48 )} = \frac{17.091903...}{\sin ( 118 )}$

**[1]**

> *Multiply both sides by sin(48) and type into your calculator.*

$\begin{gathered} x = \frac{17.091903...}{\sin ( 118 )} \times \sin ( 48 ) \\ = 14.385632... \end{gathered}$

> *Round to 1 decimal place. Remember to include units for the length.*

$AB=14.4m(1\mathrm{dp})$* ***[1]**

parts.solutionMd:
> *The parallelogram is split into two identical triangles. To use the formula for the area of a triangle you need two sides and the angle between them. You do not currently have this so use triangle **ACD** to help find the required angle.*

![4-11-edexcel-gcse-vhq3](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/SyllabAI/syllabai-resources/3b2ce8da700b80f51700fb34fc721c90d6654d6b/SME-ExamQuestion/cie-igcse-maths-international-maths-23-extended/pythagoras-and-trigonometry/sine-cosine-rule-and-area-of-triangles/assets/048-4-11-edexcel-gcse-vhq3.png)

> *You know the length of one side and the angle opposite it. You also know the length of another side so you can use the sine rule to find the angle opposite it.*

> *The formula for the sine rule is *$\frac{\mathrm{sin}A}{a}=\frac{\mathrm{sin}B}{b}$*, where **a** and **b** are the lengths of the two sides that are opposite the angles **A **and **B **respectively. *

> *Substitute **a** = **9**, **b** = 11, **A** = **y** and **B** = 100 into the formula.*

$\frac{\sin ( y )}{9} = \frac{\sin ( 100 )}{11}$

**[1]**

> *Multiply both sides by 9 and then find the angle by using the inverse sin function.*

$\begin{gathered} \sin ( y ) & = \frac{\sin ( 100 )}{11} \times 9 \\ y = \sin ^{- 1} ( \frac{\sin ( 100 )}{11} \times 9 ) \end{gathered}$

**[1]**

> *Type into your calculator.*

$\begin{gathered} y = 53.682923... \end{gathered}$

> *You can find the third angle by spotting that the three interior angles of the triangle should add up to 180°. Use the answer button on your calculator.*

$\begin{gathered} x = 180 - 100 - 53.682923... \\ = 26.317076... \end{gathered}$

**[1]**

> *You now have enough information to find the area of one of the triangles.*

> *The formula for the area of a triangle is *$\mathrm{Area}=\frac{1}{2}ab\mathrm{sin}C$*, where **a** and **b** are the lengths of the two sides that form angle **C**. Substitute **a** = 9, **b** = 11 and **C** = 26.317076... (using the answer button) into the formula.*

$\begin{gathered} \text{Area} = 1 \frac{1}{2} \times 9 \times 11 \times \sin ( 26.317076... ) \\ = 21.945249... \end{gathered}$

**[1]**

> *Multiply by 2 to find the area of the parallelogram.*

$\begin{gathered} 2 \times 21.945249... & = 43.890498... \end{gathered}$

> *Round to 3 significant figures. Remember to include square units for the area.*

$\mathrm{Area}=43.9\mathrm{cm}^{2}(3\mathrm{sf})$** [1]**

**[1]**

> * Substitute **a** = **y**, **b** = 8, **c** = 8 and **A** = 40.005200... (using the answer button) into the formula.*

parts.problemMd:
The frequency table shows information about the number of books read by some students in a reading marathon.

| Number of books read | $1$ | $2$ | $3$ | $4$ | $5$ | $6$ | $7$ | $8$ |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Frequency | $2$ | $2$ | $16$ | $10$ | $9$ | $4$ | $x$ | $2$ |

i) The mean number of books read is 4.28.

Find the value of $x$.

$x=$.................................................. [3]

ii) Write down the mode.

[1]

iii) Write down the median.

[1]
parts.solutionMd:
i) *For each option, find the total number of books read by multiplying the number of books by the frequency*

| Number of books read | $1$ | $2$ | $3$ | $4$ | $5$ | $6$ | $7$ | $8$ |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Frequency | $2$ | $2$ | $16$ | $10$ | $9$ | $4$ | $x$ | $2$ |
| *Total number of books read* | *2* | *4* | *48* | *40* | *45* | *24* | $7x$ | *16* |

> *Find an expression for the total number of books read by adding together all the totals*

> *Simplify the expression*

$2+4+48+40+45+24+7x+16=7x+179$

**[1]**

> *Find an expression for the total frequency by adding together all the frequencies*

> *Simplify the expression*

$2+2+16+10+9+4+x+2=x+45$

> *The mean is the total number of books read divided by the total frequency*

> *Use the given mean to form an equation*

$\frac{7x+179}{x+45}=4.28$

**[1]**

> *Multiply both sides by *$x+45$* and expand*

$\begin{gathered} 7 x + 179 & = 4.28 ( x + 45 ) \\ 7 x + 179 & = 4.28 x + 192.6 \end{gathered}$

> *Rearrange to get all the **x** terms on one side by themselves*

> *Subtract 4.28**x** from both sides and subtract 179 from both sides*

> *Simplify both sides*

$\begin{gathered} 7 x - 4.28 x & = 192.6 - 179 \\ 2.72 x & = 13.6 \end{gathered}$

> *Divide both sides by 2.72*

$x=\frac{13.6}{2.72}$

$x=5$ **[1]**

ii) *The mode is the option with the highest frequency*

**Mode is 3 books** **[1]**

iii) *Find the total frequency by substituting *$x=5$* into the expression from part (a) *$x+45.$

$5+45=50$

> *The median is the middle value when the values are in order from smallest to biggest*

> *Instead of writing out all 50 values, you can consider where the middle would be*

> *The median is the midpoint between the 25*<sup>*th*</sup>* and 26*<sup>*th*</sup>* values*

> *Find the cumulative frequencies*

| Number of books read | $1$ | $2$ | $3$ | $4$ | $5$ | $6$ | $7$ | $8$ |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| *Cumulative Frequency* | *2* | *4* | *20* | *30* | *39* | *43* | *48* | *50* |

> *Both the 25*<sup>*th*</sup>* and 26*<sup>*th*</sup>* values are 4 so the midpoint between them is also 4*

**Median is 4 books** **[1]**

[2]
parts.solutionMd:
i) *In the first class interval the cumulative frequency will be the same as the frequency. *
*In subsequent class intervals, add the frequency to the cumulative frequency of the previous class interval.*

| Time ($t$ minutes) | $20<t\leq25$ | $25<t\leq30$ | $30<t\leq35$ | $35<t\leq40$ | $40<t\leq45$ |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Frequency | 44 | 32 | 28 | 12 | 4 |

**following this method with one error**** [1]**

| Time ($t$ minutes) | $t\leq20$ | $t\leq25$ | $t\leq30$ | $t\leq35$ | $t\leq40$ | $t\leq45$ |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Cumulative frequency | $0$ | $44$ | **Final answer:** **76** | **Final answer:** **104** | **Final answer:** **116** | **Final answer:** **120** |

**[1]**

ii) *No students had a time of less than 20 minutes. So plot the first point at (20, 0). *
*44 students had a time of 25 minutes or less so plot the next point at (25, 44) on the grid, and so on to (45, 120), plotting at the **upper** bound of each class interval. *
*After plotting all six points, join them up with a smooth curve.*

* The UQ is three-quarters of the way along 120 students, so the (120 ÷ 4 x 3 =) "90*<sup>*th*</sup>* student". *

*UQ = 32.5*

> *Use your graphical display calculator in statistics mode to enter the data into columns*

> *Choose the option for linear regression, or you may need to press CALC then REG*

$y=0.28+0.194857142...x$

parts.problemMd:
The pie charts give information about the ages, in years, of people living in two towns, Adley and Bridford.

![q1-1-hard-6-2-statistical-diagrams-edexcel-gcse-maths](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/SyllabAI/syllabai-resources/3b2ce8da700b80f51700fb34fc721c90d6654d6b/SME-ExamQuestion/cie-igcse-maths-international-maths-23-extended/statistics/statistical-diagrams/assets/005-q1-1-hard-6-2-statistical-diagrams-edexcel-gcse-.png)

The ratio of the number of people living in Adley to the number of people living in Bridford is given by the ratio of the areas of the pie charts.

What proportion of the total number of people living in these two towns live in Adley **and** are aged 0 -19? 
Give your answer correct to 3 significant figures.
parts.solutionMd:
> *As the diagrams are drawn accurately we can measure the radius of each pie chart and use these to find the ratio of the areas (and so the populations) of Adley and Bridford.*

![6-2-hard-q1-1](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/SyllabAI/syllabai-resources/3b2ce8da700b80f51700fb34fc721c90d6654d6b/SME-ExamQuestion/cie-igcse-maths-international-maths-23-extended/statistics/statistical-diagrams/assets/007-6-2-hard-q1-1.png)

> *The area of a circle is given by the formula *$A=πr^{2}$*.*

*Area of Adley pie chart*$= \mathrm{\pi } ( 5 )^{2} = 25 \mathrm{\pi }$

**[1]**

*Area of Bridford pie chart*$= \mathrm{\pi } ( 4 )^{2} = 16 \mathrm{\pi }$

> *So the ratio of the populations of Adley to Bridford (*$A:B$*) is*

$A:B=25π:16π=25:16$

> *and so the fraction of people living in Adley is*

$\frac{25}{25+16}=\frac{25}{41}$

> *Measure the angle of the 0 - 19 category on the Adley pie chart so we can work out the fraction of people living in Adley who are aged 0 - 19.*

![6-2-hard-q1-2](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/SyllabAI/syllabai-resources/3b2ce8da700b80f51700fb34fc721c90d6654d6b/SME-ExamQuestion/cie-igcse-maths-international-maths-23-extended/statistics/statistical-diagrams/assets/008-6-2-hard-q1-2.png)

$\frac{70}{360}=\frac{7}{36}$

> *To find the proportion of people (out of the two towns) who live in Adley **AND** are aged 0 - 19 we need to find the product of these two fractions.*

$\frac{25}{41}\times\frac{7}{36}=\frac{175}{1476}$

**[1]**

*This is an awkward fraction so the answer is best given as a percentage.* 
*To change *$\frac{175}{1476}$* to a percentage use your calculator to convert it to a decimal, and then multiply by 100.*

$\frac{175}{1476} \times 100 \% = 11.856 ...$

> *Round your final answer to a sensible degree of accuracy, three significant figures is often used.*

**Proportion of people living in Adley and aged 0 - 19 years is 11.9% (3 s.f.)** **[1]**

$n=\frac{55}{22}=\frac{5}{2}$
